The UK is set to witness its fullest solar eclipse for the next 54 years this Wednesday, with the Met Office pinpointing Devon and Cornwall as prime locations for viewing the celestial event.

Between 6.17pm and 8.06pm on August 12, over 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon.

It will be the most extensive blockage of the sun over British skies since the total eclipse of 1999.

The south-west of England, specifically Devon and Cornwall, and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire in Wales, are forecast to experience the fullest extent of the eclipse, with 94 to 96 per cent of the sun expected to be covered.

Plymouth, for instance, is predicted to see 94.66 per cent obscuration at 7.16pm.

Elsewhere, regions including the rest of Wales, Northern Ireland, parts of the West Midlands and the wider South West, and western Scotland, can anticipate between 92 and 94 per cent solar coverage.

open image in gallery The Met Office has released a map showing the best places to watch the 2026 solar eclipse ( Met Office )

Cardiff is expected to see 93.24 per cent of the sun obscured at 7.13pm, while Belfast will experience 93.09 per cent coverage at 7.08pm.

Skygazers in the rest of the UK will likely see the moon obscure 90 per cent to 92 per cent of the sun – with 91.79 per cent expected in Birmingham at 7.12pm, 91.41 per cent in London at 7.13pm, 90.74 per cent in Inverness at 7.03pm, 90.71 per cent in Edinburgh at 7.06pm and 90.22 per cent in Newcastle at 7.07pm.

Those keen to catch a sight of the fullest possible solar eclipse should avoid the easternmost parts of the UK, where only 88 per cent to 90 per cent of solar coverage is expected.

These include the coasts of Norfolk, Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire, as well as the Orkney and Shetland Islands.

open image in gallery Planetarium Astronomer Dr Carys Herbert demonstrates wearing Celestron solar eclipse glasses to safely view the celestial event ( PA )

Do I need glasses to view the solar eclipse?

The Royal Greenwich Observatory warned the public that regular sunglasses are not a safe enough method to view the cosmic phenomenon.

Imo Bell, a planetarium astronomer at the observatory, previously said: “It’s not a total eclipse, but over 90 per cent is really exciting. We’re not going to get one this good for a really long time.

“So, it’s important not to miss it, and to be prepared. You can’t just go out and expect to have a look because it’s really dangerous for your eyes.

“So, you can use solar eclipse glasses, which are very, very different from sunglasses – they block out so much light that you can’t see anything through them except the sun, because that’s how much light they need to block for the damaging light of the sun to be safe to view.

“Ideally a solar telescope is an amazing way to witness it, and if you don’t have one of them then you can look into whether your local astronomy society is doing any events.

“And if all else fails, you can project the image of the eclipse using a household item like a colander which has lots of holes in – point the colander towards the Sun with your back facing it, and in the shadow of the colander you’ll be able to see the eclipse in the holes, which is really cool.”

The next time the moon obscures as much of the sun will be in 2081 and the next total solar eclipse in the UK will be in 2090.

Ms Bell advised getting to a vantage point facing west, with minimal buildings around, as the best way to view the eclipse.

“We might notice the sky getting a little bit dark, so if you’re looking safely, it’ll look a bit like the moon is taking a bite out of the sun, you’ll see something that looks a bit like a crescent sun.”

The Red Arrows have been forced to pull out of a number of summer events in the UK after poor weather left them stranded in Canada.

The Royal Air Force (RAF) aerobatics display team are a popular fixture at air shows and military events around the country during the summer but they will not be able to fulfil three forthcoming engagements as their return across the Atlantic has been delayed.

They will not be performing at the Eastbourne International Airshow (13-16 August), the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo (ongoing until 29 August) and Lyme Regis Lifeboat Week (15-22 August).

open image in gallery The Red Arrows are a fixture of summer air shows ( AFP/Getty )

The Red Arrows’ single-engine Hawk aircraft have a limited range and cannot carry out air-to-air refuelling, the RAF said.

As such, crossing the Atlantic has to be done in stages and requires having the correct RAF support aircraft, including search-and-rescue cover and those carrying essential technical equipment, in the right place, at the right time.

Weather in north-east Canada has been “particularly challenging”, the air force said, adding that the team will now have to begin its multi-leg journey back to the UK from next week.

Other RAF aircraft will participate at the events in the UK.

open image in gallery The RAF Red Arrows have had to pull out of a string of summer events ( PA )

The Typhoon Display Team and Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (BBMF) remain part of the line-up at Eastbourne.

The BBMF is also carrying out flypasts at Lyme Regis during Lifeboat Week, on 21 and 22 August.

A C-17 Globemaster and two Typhoon jets will now perform a flypast over the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo on Saturday 15 August.

open image in gallery The Red Arrows perform a flypast over Windsor Castle during a state visit for US President Donald Trump on September 17, 2025 ( Getty )

A statement on the RAF website said: “The Red Arrows plan to continue a multi-leg journey back to the United Kingdom from North America next week (w/c 10 August).

“Due to a prolonged period of poor weather in the north-eastern regions of Canada, the team’s return from a tour of the United States was postponed last week.

“It is now anticipated this Atlantic crossing will be able to begin again from late next week based on more favourable conditions.

“Regrettably, this revised timeline means the Red Arrows will not be in a position to complete performances at Airbourne: Eastbourne International Airshow, the Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo and Lyme Regis Lifeboat Week.

open image in gallery The the Red Arrows fly over the Mall towards from Buckingham Palace following the armed forces procession on 5 May 2025 to celebrate the 80th anniversary of VE Day ( AFP/Getty )

“All of these events remain on as scheduled with exciting line-ups and featuring other participating RAF aircraft.

Wing commander Sasha Nash, officer commanding RAF Aerobatic Team, added: “We are very sorry the Red Arrows cannot participate at these events and we are grateful to organisers and communities for their understanding.

“Every effort is being made to ensure the Red Arrows can recommence the busy display season as soon as possible.

“However, safety is the only factor that will determine the timing of the team’s return from Canada.”

The UK economy is expected to have recorded another quarter of growth as businesses find ways to cope with the fallout of the Iran war, but some industries are coming under increasing pressure, economists think.

Figures from the Office for National Statistics published on Thursday are set to show a degree of resilience in the economy in the face of supply chain issues and price pressures linked to the conflict, as well as a period of political uncertainty.

Some economists think gross domestic product (GDP) will have increased 0.4% for the second quarter, between April and June.

This would mean the economy has continued growing after a 0.6% rise in GDP for the first three months of 2026.

Rob Wood, chief UK economist for Pantheon Macroeconomics, said this would show “the big picture is that the economy has remained resilient to the hit from the war in Iran”.

open image in gallery

It comes as the services sector – the most dominant in the UK economy – strengthened in May, largely coming from professional services and scientific research and development.

Furthermore, recent data has pointed to factories and manufacturing firms stockpiling in anticipation of supply shortages and price rises, which has helped keep growth elevated.

But a weaker picture may be emerging from June as the heatwaves bring mixed results for businesses and some industries come under increasing pressure, economists said.

Mr Wood is expecting monthly GDP to dip by 0.1% in June, “reversing the 0.1% gain in May, as a sharp fall in construction activity drags on growth, while services and industrial production stagnate”.

open image in gallery England reaching the World Cup semi-finals is expected to have helped boost spending in July (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Thomas Pugh, chief economist for RSM UK, said he was expecting the services industry to have been dragged down by a fall in hospitality activity, despite the Fifa World Cup kicking off in June.

Mr Pugh said its own business surveys suggest “consumers were likely switching away from restaurants towards pubs to watch the World Cup, rather than increasing the total amount of spending”.

But he added: “There could still be a boost to activity in July, given the scorching weather and England reaching the semi-finals.”

Mr Pugh has a slightly more positive outlook for June, forecasting monthly GDP to have risen by 0.1%.

“All told, we expect GDP to nudge up in June, helped by a big jump in erratic mining activity,” he said.

“That will be enough to deliver 0.4% growth for Q2 (the second quarter), as strong momentum from Q1 (the first quarter) and consumers smoothing through higher inflation helped to support solid growth.”

A quarterly increase in GDP will likely be good news for new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has said he wants to achieve “growth in every postcode” of the UK.

He opened a new headquarters for the centre of Government in Manchester in late July, named No 10 North, where he is expected to work once each week as part of his move to push power out of Westminster.

Filip Nowacki admitted celebrating a breakout Commonwealth Games in Glasgow has been the farthest thing from his mind as he gears up for the European Aquatics Championships in Paris this week.

It has been a whirlwind past couple of weeks for the teenager, who claimed silver in the men’s 100 metres breaststroke, nudging mentor and three-time Olympic champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty into bronze.

Nowacki then went one better in his preferred 200m breaststroke, beating 2020 Olympic gold medallist Zac Stubblety-Cook, but the 18-year-old has barely had a chance to reflect on his seismic achievements.

Instead, Nowacki is targeting European honours, getting his campaign under way on Monday in the 100m breaststroke alongside Ramsay-Peaty, and he accepts that is part and parcel of a swimmer’s lot.

“No time to celebrate,” Nowacki told the Press Association. “After the Commonwealth Games, it’s always quite hard to settle back down to reality and it’s very important you do that as fast as possible.

“Because living on a high and living on that emotion is very taxing and it takes a lot of energy out of the system so now it’s just about recovering and getting the mind straight before diving back into it.

“Ultimately, all the hard work in the season has been put in, I can’t change how I’m going to swim apart from making sure my body’s fresh and my mind’s ready to go.”

Nowacki, the world junior 100m and 200m breaststroke champion, became the most decorated athlete in Jersey’s Commonwealth Games history with his two medals, claiming the island’s first gold in 36 years.

“I’m very proud of myself,” he said. “To step up on a senior international stage is challenging and there was a lot of pressure from Jersey that I didn’t quite feel beforehand.

open image in gallery Leon Marchand has withdrawn from the men’s 200 metres breaststroke in Paris this week (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Archive )

“But after both my races, I stepped back into my hotel room and I could finally breathe again – it was a massive weight off my shoulders, which I didn’t realise I had in the first place.”

A mouthwatering clash with Leon Marchand awaited Nowacki in the 200m breaststroke on Wednesday and Thursday, but an adductor injury has led to the four-time Olympic champion pulling out of the event.

“I’d love to race against him,” Nowacki said. “I’m always up for a race and that’s what’s very special: I get to race against the best in the world.”

While Nowacki will once again go up against Ramsay-Peaty in the 100m breaststroke, he clearly reveres the world record holder and takes every opportunity to speak to him in an effort to learn from him.

“I’ve looked up to him since he won his first Olympic gold medal in 2016, I must have been eight or nine and watching the replays on TV was special,” Nowacki added.

open image in gallery Adam Ramsay-Peaty will also be in action in the French capital this week (Andrew Milligan/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It’s nice to be racing against him in the lane next to him. I’ve got pictures of us both swimming breaststroke, an underwater shot, and I think that’s really cool. Had you told me that two years ago, I would have shaken my head in disbelief.

“He’s definitely played a massive role in my character development, especially from last year. I’ve spoken to him multiple times and I always try to extract as much experience from him as I can.”

Spanish authorities have announced the dismantling of a major people-smuggling operation, believed to have trafficked more than 2,000 migrants into the country and generated profits of €24 million (£20.5 million).

The network, described by Spain's Civil Guard as "one of the most complex, active and dangerous transnational criminal networks detected to date in the Mediterranean", used speedboats to transport synthetic drugs from Spain to Algeria.

On their return journeys, the boats then smuggled migrants to Spain's southeastern coast and the island of Ibiza.

The announcement comes as migration and human trafficking remain pressing concerns across Spain and Europe, following a mass border crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in late July, which saw 72,000 people enter the city.

Tens of thousands have since returned to Morocco, with many of those left behind setting up camp on the beach, while authorities have reported that the migrant reception centres in the city are overwhelmed.

Police believe the group, known for employing "extreme violence to protect its vessels", carried out at least 64 smuggling operations.

Members of the Spanish Guardia Civil patrol and conduct searches near a floating barrier off the border with Morocco ( Reuters )

Although the number of irregular migrants reaching Spain by sea fell 31 per cent in January-July, this was largely due to a 60 per cent drop in arrivals to the Canary Islands, Interior Ministry data showed.

By contrast, irregular migration to mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands rose 22 per cent and 10 per cent, respectively, over the same period as smugglers shifted routes via Algeria.

During the investigation, conducted with Europol and police in France, Portugal and Poland, authorities seized 18 speedboats and arrested 77 people in Spain and one in Algeria.

The network charged up to €12,000 (£10,000) per migrant and transported as many as 50 people on a single crossing, according to the statement.

The sea crossings were extremely dangerous, the Civil Guard said, with migrants travelling in overcrowded boats at high speed and often in rough seas, without lights, and, in most cases, life jackets.

"Sometimes the occupants were even tied down to prevent them from falling overboard during the crossing," the police said, adding that the organisation perpetrated extraordinary levels of violence against its own members and the migrants, as well as against police forces.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner. I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday as officials declared a state of emergency.

The fire in Bald Range doubled in size overnight on Friday, spreading rapidly to about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across British Columbia, including Summerland, Peachland and other districts west of Okanagan Lake.

The region produces most of British Columbia’s wine and is Canada’s second-largest wine-producing area.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas ready to be ‘pushed to the limit’ in debut WSL season after stunning London City Lionesses free transfer
Sports.content:
ALEXIA PUTELLAS is prepared to be pushed to the limit in her debut WSL campaign.

The 32-year-old completed a stunning free transfer to London City Lionesses last month after ending her trophy-laden 14-year stay with Barcelona.



Now she is gearing up for a completely new challenge in what she considers to be one of the most competitive leagues in the world.

Putellas said: “You never know which will be the result of the game, so it’s a very competitive league week after week.



“We haven’t started [the season] yet but if I have to imagine all the games will push you to your limit. It’s a very entertaining league. That’s a key point for the fans.”

Having swapped Barcelona for Bromley, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner is now eager to develop further as a player – despite having already won 40 major trophies.



She continued: “It will be different for sure but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving as a footballer, as a person as well.

“It’s being more of a complete player as much as I can, so learning new things, playing with and against other players, just trying to find where my limits are.

“It will take time because, of course, it’s a new beginning, a big change for me but I’m so excited to be here.”

Putellas had extensive conversations with London City owner Michele Kang prior to making the move and was particularly impressed by the ambition of the club.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

London City Lionesses were only promoted to the WSL last year, but Kang has plans to develop them into a European powerhouse.

Putellas added: “The first conversation was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete.

“I made the move for that and just being in another position that I’ve never been in and in my opinion this league can give me that.

“Always, day after day, I want to learn things. I’m learning new things and that’s the way I see this job. Just keep going, never be stopped and be as better as I can.”



As well as speaking to Kang, Putellas also got in contact with former Barcelona team-mates Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze – both now at Chelsea – who briefed her on life in England.

“Some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re gonna kick me,” she laughed. “No, just joking!

“But no problem, I’m ready for that or I’m trying to be ready. Just enjoy the league because the games are crazy and even if you go for an away game it’s like something’s different, something special and I’m ready for enjoying all of that and being ready for what the games will be for me.”

Putellas could make her debut on the opening day of the season when London City Lionesses host Manchester United on September 4 at the Copperjax Community Stadium.

Sports.title: Will Bruno Guimaraes play for Arsenal against Borussia Dortmund today in Emirates Cup?
Sports.content:
ARSENAL finally got Brazilian sensation Bruno Guimaraes over the line – and fans could see him get a run out earlier than expected!

Guimaraes, 28, signed a four-year deal with an option to extend until 2031 after completing his medical on Thursday.

Newcastle had been reluctant to sell their skipper but they caved in after the Gunners offered to pay the full £75million fee up front.



After his arrival, Bruno said: “Like I said, I’m your warrior, I’ll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.”



And those memories could start from today’s pre-season match where Arsenal take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

Will Bruno Guimaraes play for Arsenal today?

It has not yet been confirmed whether Bruno Guimaraes will make his first appearance in an Arsenal shirt today.

The midfield maestro is still short of fitness as he was given a mandatory three-week break following his involvement with Brazil at the World Cup.



However, reports suggest that Bruno has already been training with his new Gunners team-mates so there could be a slight chance.

Guimaraes is Arsenal’s third signing after Ilan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.

What has Bruno Guimaraes said?

The Brazilian star said: “Well, I feel good, I feel amazing. I’m glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to [Arsenal sporting director Andrea] Berta and Mikel [Arteta], I was excited.

“I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.



“I’m so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here. I’m so excited to meet the other players, to start training. I just want to give my best.

“I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it. I’m so excited to start.

“We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Sports.title: EFL star shown straight red card for PUNCHING 17-year-old rival in moment of madness
Sports.content:
BOLTON WANDERERS midfielder Xavier Simons made a shocking start to the season after being sent off for PUNCHING Sheffield Wednesday teenager Harry Gray.

The former Chelsea youngster, 23, then saw his side crash out of the Carabao Cup following his moment of madness.



Bolton won promotion to the Championship after thumping Stockport in the League One play-off final in May.

And they made the trip to Hillsborough looking to book their place in the second round of the Carabao Cup.



But Bolton were reduced to ten men in the early stages of the second half as Simons was shown a straight red card.

The defensive midfielder lashed out at Gray, who has joined Sheffield Wednesday on loan from Leeds, after his shirt was tugged.



Simons sensationally punched his 17-year-old rival in the stomach, leading to a scuffle.

Sports.title: Fans left stunned as wayward clearance causes terrifying CAR CRASH on live TV during football match
Sports.content:
A URUGUAYAN football match caused chaos when a wayward clearance sensationally led to a horrifying car crash.

Uruguay Montevideo and Paysandu locked horns in a Segunda Division Profesional clash at the tiny Estadio Parque ANCAP yesterday.



And the home side’s Richard Nunez inadvertently put those outside the arena in danger when he stopped a promising counter-attack.

Paysandu were looking to bag the showdown’s opener after quickly breaking away following a poor Uruguay Montevideo corner.



Nunez ended those hopes by rushing across and thumping the ball onto a busy road.

But the defender’s no-nonsense clearance caused a terrifying car accident – with one vehicle smashing into the back of another.



Although no injuries were caused by the crash, traffic was stopped for 20 minutes.

The shocking moment was captured on live TV and had fans racing onto social media.

One said: “A car slammed on the brakes to avoid hitting it and got rear-ended. Pure South American football.”

Another added: “One of the most crazy things I’ve ever seen.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A third chimed in: “Unbelievable.”

A fourth cheekily claimed: “Go explain to your boss that a wild clearance from the Uruguay Montevideo defender made you crash and that’s why you were late.”

A fifth questioned: “What will they tell the insurance company?”

Uruguay Montevideo went on to notch a 1-0 win following the unexpected incident.

Lucas Rodriguez bagged what proved to be the only goal of the contest just before half-time.



The slender victory allowed Uruguay Montevideo to move up to eighth place in the Segunda Division Profesional and they are now seven points adrift of table-topping Plaza Colonia.

Sports.title: ‘I felt that’ – Fans wince as skydiver CRASHES into advertising boards in painful moment as football teams left stunned

What was supposed to be entertainment descended into chaos as a parachuter soared into the advertising boards with some force.



Dutch side Go Ahead Eagles had planned an unorthodox delivery of the match ball for their Eredivisie opener against Willem II.

The plan was for a team of skydivers to glide down and place the ball in the centre spot.



However, while there was a team of parachutists, one stood out as he uncontrollably flew towards the pitch.

He ended up smashing into the goal stanchion and the advertising boards in an embarrassing stunt.

The commentator saw the funny side of the incident as he said: “The first injury of the season is a fact, not of a player, but a parachutist.”

Sports.title: Prem icon backs Jaissle to shine at Newcastle despite Guimaraes, Tonali & Gordon transfers and says Woltemade will star
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE will instantly get Newcastle fighting for Europe again despite the exodus of stars from the club.

And marmite striker Nick Woltemade is the ideal man to provide the goals for a top-eight finish.



Odds dropped on Newcastle being relegated this week after captain Bruno Guimaraes joined Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon in heading out the exit door.

Jaissle looks to have a huge job on his hands, especially with all three of the Mags’ outfield signings being 20 or younger, to improve on Eddie Howe’s disappointing 12th place finish last season.



Howe himself no longer had the energy for a rebuild and left last week. But former Toon midfielder Dietmar Hamann is adamant that despite the chaos it is a “very good time” for his German compatriot to take over.

Speaking exclusively to Sun Sport via MrQ Casino ahead of Toon’s 2-1 win vs Valencia on Saturday, he said: “Expectations have probably come down a little bit because they went north very quickly with the Saudis taking over a few years ago, and now there’s a chance to go again.



“Eddie did a very good job in getting them into the Champions League and winning the Carabao Cup but now it’s probably time for somebody else to take over and maybe go that next step.

“Newcastle fans will always have fond memories of Eddie Howe, will always have a place in their hearts for him. But it’s a very good time for a new manager to take over there now.”

Jaissle took charge for the first time in a friendly against Valencia at the Mestalla on Saturday. And after a week’s training camp in La Manga, he has just a fortnight to get his men ready to face Liverpool in a bumper Prem opener.

But even though there are many doubters, Hamann is convinced they will be in the fight for Europe come May.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “I’d say a top eight finish because he’s still got some very good players in Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw at the back. And Joelinton is very capable. So there are still some experienced players there, even though some of them are still pretty young in football terms. They’ve got the capabilities to finish well.

“What Jaissle did in Salzburg is he gave young players a chance. He gave them responsibility and, more often than not, they paid him back with performances.

“This is the way to go. this is the way he wants to play as well, a very high intensity game where you need a pretty young team. It fits pretty well.



“The players they bought have got a manager who trusts them. Jaissle is different because he likes to give them a chance. He showed that in Salzburg. So it’s a very good fit for this particular time at Newcastle.”

Much-maligned club-record signing Woltemade arrived with a bang last summer before the goals dried and he was shifted back into a No10 and midfield role last term. The drop-off in form also cost him his place in Germany’s side for the World Cup.

But Hamann has every confidence things will click for him on Tyneside.

He added: “The way Jaissle likes to play always suits a target man like Woltemade. I was very surprised when he started the season so well and then disappeared for pretty much the rest of it.

“There were reports that he’s not settled in Newcastle, which I can’t really understand because there aren’t many better football cities in England, let alone in Europe.

“Woltemade’s a very capable player, technically very gifted and brings others into play. It’s very important to have quick players around him. He had that with Gordon last season.

“That’s why there’s probably one or two more incoming. Hopefully, we then see the Woltemade we saw at the start of last season, not just for a three-month spell, but for the full campaign.”

Sports.title: Phil Foden’s girlfriend flogging Three Lions shirts on Vinted after he was dropped by Tuchel
Sports.content:
SNUBBED England ace Phil Foden’s girlfriend is flogging new Three Lions shirts on Vinted — after her World Cup trip with other Wags did not go ahead.

Rebecca Cooke, 25, offers two shirts on the second-hand website for £70 each — the latest white home and red away strips.



The jerseys were modified by a clothing brand which tightened the waists for women.

Other England Wags who did make it to the US and Mexico for the World Cup wore the same tops — including Ollie Watkins’ wife Ellie and Anthony Gordon’s girlfriend Annie Keating.



The tops — both in size 12-14 — are listed as being “new with tags”.

They have been modified by Essex-based company A Vintage Fit.

The shirts cost £89.99 on the official England website and the firm charges £90 each to adapt them into a figure-hugging version.

Mum-of-three Rebecca’s England tops are among more than 100 items for sale on her Vinted page.

Also included are four cinched Man City tops — including last season’s grey and bright green third kit for £70 in “perfect condition”.

Two City shirts are vintage from retro footie kit firm Score Draw.



Rebecca’s account states: “Selling new & used authentic items only. Account ran by management team.”



It was not known if she donates to charity any money raised through Vinted.

She had been expecting to go to this year’s World Cup tournament with £15million-a-year Man City star Phil, 26.

He was devastated at being dropped by manager Thomas Tuchel.

A source said: “Perhaps Rebecca had one foot on the plane when she got the tops.”

We approached Rebecca and Phil for comment.



Under-fire Fifa boss Gianni Infantino was last night facing new pressure after it was alleged he paid off a mistress in his job as a Uefa executive.

He denies the allegations.

Sports.title: West Ham have reasons for optimism despite relegation but hard work isn't over
Sports.content:
West Ham have reasons for optimism despite relegation but hard work isn't over

Nuno Espirito Santo is targeting promotion with West Ham but there is still work to do in the lead-up to their Championship opener

View 3 Images There is still reason for hope about West Ham (Image: Getty)

West Ham United might be playing in a lower division than this time last year but there's some optimism around the London Stadium. However, a lack of summer signings means some concerns remain.

‌



Positivity is a strange feeling given the pain of relegation in May. And yet there are reasons to be cheerful - not least Jarrod Bowen's decision to stay.

‌



Club captain Bowen narrowly missed out on a place in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad and was linked with an instant Premier League return. But the former Hull City forward was convinced to stay and lead a promotion charge after meeting with Hammers chiefs.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I did an interview after [the final game of last season] and said my vision is to get this club back in the Premier League," Bowen said in July when announcing he was staying. "Sometimes you think it falls on deaf ears and people say 'he's just saying that'.

"But when I say something, I don't hide away from it. It was a no-brainer for me to be here and the vision is clear, it's the Premier League."

‌



View 3 Images Nuno has agreed to stay on as manager (Image: PA)

The last time Bowen was in the Championship, he was the seventh-highest scorer in the division despite leaving Hull for West Ham mid-season. And he isn't the only one hoping to call upon expertise at this level to lead the Hammers back up at the first time of asking.

Nuno Espirito Santo couldn't keep the team in the top flight, though there was a notable improvement after he was allowed to bring in some of his own signings in January. The Portuguese coach has already won the Championship once before, albeit nearly a decade ago with Wolves, and is ready to target another title.

‌



There has been some uncertainty behind the scenes, with joint-chair David Sullivan stepping down and a consortium including Amanda Staveley now looking to take a stake in the club. But the Hammers have insisted this won't affect day-to-day affairs.

West Ham know they will be there to be got at, though, and need to keep their focus. Experience at this level can help, with Kyle Walker-Peters and Mads Hermansen both earning promotion to the Premier League in recent years.

"The other teams will make it difficult for us, but we just have to focus on ourselves, do our work and be confident," said full-back Walker-Peters, who came up with Southampton in 2024.

Nuno's decision to stay could well be a factor in convincing important players to follow suit. Taty Castellanos joined from Lazio for £25m and scored six goals in 18 games, but has been a fixture in pre-season and there's still hope he stays put.

Efforts are also being made to keep hold of last season's Hammer of the Year, Dinos Mavropanos, despite Premier League interest. There is even faint hope that Axel Disasi, so impressive on loan last season, can be convinced to drop down a division.

‌



View 3 Images West Ham have lost key players like Fernandes (Image: Getty)

Of course, there have been some sales which naturally follow a drop down to the second tier. The departure of academy graduate Freddie Potts hasn't gone down well with everyone. But bringing in well above £100m for Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville should mean the club can be more selective when it comes to future sales.

Callum Wilson and Adama Traore have left for free and other high earners such as Jean-Clair Todibo and Niclas Fullkrug could also soon leave. Then there's the lack of new faces. Keiber Lamadrid - on loan last season but used just once by Nuno - was the only senior signing as July ticked into August, though Joel Veltman has since followed.

Article continues below

Still, it's worth remembering this is a squad which picked up 39 points in the Premier League last season and gave title-winners Arsenal a real fright in May. The challenge now is to rebuild with Bowen at the core and time is running out to get the necessary deals over the line.

Sports.title: 'I negotiated Man Utd transfer – they paid more than double what we expected'
Sports.content:
'I negotiated Man Utd transfer – they paid more than double what we expected'

One of Manchester United's most high-profile signings ended up leaving the selling club delighted with the fee they received

View 2 Images Luke Shaw's move from Southampton to Manchester United in 2014 was blockbuster (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Former Southampton chief Les Reed claims he "pulled Manchester United's pants down" during negotiations for Luke Shaw after selling the defender for more than double the amount the club had expected to receive.

‌



In 2014, Shaw became the most expensive teenager in world football after joining United in a £30million deal. At the time, the transfer was viewed as something of a coup for the Red Devils, who had beaten off competition from several Premier League rivals to land one of the most highly-rated young talents in Europe.

‌



But ultimately, it was Southampton who came away from negotiations rubbing their hands together. Recalling the transfer on the Fozcast podcast after being asked by Ben Foster whether there were any deals where he felt he had got the better of another club, Reed said: "I met with Ed Woodward for the Luke Shaw transfer.

‌



"I came back to the Southampton offices and my office is on the same floor as the finance director and the chief executive. And they had their doors open and we were chatting.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

7 Man Utd players face uncertain futures as part of huge summer overhaul of squad READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

"They've both gone, 'So, how much [did you sell him for]?' And I went, 'Go on, guess.' So the finance director said £12m and the CEO said, 'Nah nah, more than that. £15m.' And I said, 'Nah, you're both wrong. £30m.' I thought I've done pretty well there."

‌



The deal remains to this day Southampton's most lucrative academy sale, with Shaw having emerged from the club's famed youth system before becoming a first team regular at St Mary's as a teenager.

The full back was one of several high-profile departures overseen by Reed during his eight-year spell at Southampton, which began with him serving as Head of Football Development and Support before later becoming Vice-Chairman.

Between 2010 and 2018, he played a key role in negotiating lucrative deals for the likes of Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren, Calum Chambers, Morgan Schneiderlin, Sadio Mane and Virgil van Dijk - with those sales alone bringing in just shy of £250m for the club.

‌



View 2 Images Luke Shaw has been at Manchester United for 12 years (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Shaw would go on to establish himself as a key figure for both Manchester United and England, cementing his reputation as one of the finest left backs in Europe and ultimately justifying the fee United forked out for him.

However, injuries have repeatedly disrupted his career, with the defender making fewer than 13 Premier League appearances in five of his 12 seasons at Old Trafford.

Article continues below

Now 31, Shaw has entered the final year of his United contract and is expected to leave Old Trafford next summer, with no talks over a new deal currently taking place. Michael Carrick's side are also actively eyeing up long-term replacements for Shaw, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall high on their wish list.

Sports.title: Arsenal were snubbed for new deals by Prem winner and another Madrid star before Vini Jr
Sports.content:
Arsenal were snubbed for new deals by Prem winner and another Madrid star before Vini Jr

Arsenal failed in their pursuit of Vinicius Junior as the Brazilian pens fresh terms with Real Madrid and they've experienced similar snubs before

View 4 Images Vinicius Junior will not sign for Arsenal after agreeing to a Real Madrid extension (Image: Getty)

Arsenal have lost out on Vinicius Junior, who has penned an extension with Real Madrid. And the suggestion swirls that the Gunners' interest was used to secure these fresh, lucrative terms.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side threatened to pull off the largest coup of the summer window when they made their intentions to pursue the Real Madrid winger clear. But after crunch contract talks this week, the Brazilian will stay a Galactico until 2032.

‌



Arsenal will not get their man and it has been speculated that Vinicius used their approach to negotiate a better agreement with his Spanish employers. This is unfounded, of course, but this saga is not the only time the Gunners have gone steaming into a target, only for the player to sign a new long-term deal and stay put. Mirror Football takes a look back.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer saga reaches conclusion as Real Madrid star strikes agreement READ MORE :

Karim Benzema

In 2014, Olivier Giroud led Arsenal's line, but manager Arsene Wenger wanted an upgrade so Real Madrid star Karim Benzema was singled out. The club tried everything they could to get a deal over the line and the Frenchman, who had bagged 24 goals during the 2013/14 season, was on the verge of joining them.

However, the deal hinged on Luis Suarez leaving Liverpool for the Spanish capital. This transfer did not materialise following his World Cup biting incident and he joined Barcelona instead. Speaking to La Mesa, the Uruguayan shed light on the Benzema move that never was.

‌



View 4 Images Benzema's move to the Emirates collapsed (Image: Getty)

"My agent spoke to Real Madrid before the 2014 World Cup," Suarez said. "Madrid wanted to sign me and everything was going well. They were thinking of selling Benzema to Arsenal, everything was practically already done."

Instead, Benzema used the commotion to put pen to paper on a five-year contract extension and cemented himself as a Real great, making 648 appearances and scoring 354 goals before leaving for Al-Ittihad in 2023. He now plays for Al-Hilal.

‌



Jamie Vardy

View 4 Images Vardy snubbed the Gunners for a new Leicester deal (Image: Getty)

Two years after the Benzema ordeal, the Gunners' search for a new striker led them to approach the Premier League title-winning Jamie Vardy.

Vardy had just bagged 24 league goals to help the Foxes win the top flight and whilst he was at Euro 2016 with England, Arsenal triggered the £20million release clause in his contract.

‌



There was nothing Leicester could do and it appeared as though Vardy would become a Gunner. However, he instead signed a fresh four-year improved deal at Leicester and yet again, Arsenal were left licking their wounds.

Dayot Upamecano

Bayern Munich star Dayot Upamecano has just enjoyed a stellar World Cup with France, but six years ago, he was close to joining Arsenal.

View 4 Images Upamecano ended up at Bayern (Image: Getty)

‌



The defender was pursued quite intently by Arteta and Co. whilst he was at RB Leipzig and in July 2020, things heated up. Upamecano had just one year left on his deal and a tempting £53m release clause - a transfer looked likely.

A series of bids were rejected and then, out of nowhere, Upamecano inked a contract extension, putting an end to the speculation. To make matters worse, this deal also tactically included a clause that would make him available for £37m in one year's time.

So, in 2021, Bayern activated the bargain clause and snapped up their man, much to the dismay of Arsenal, who were yet again the victims of a brutal snub.

Liverpool's transfer window took a turn on Friday night with Andoni Iraola's Anfield bow on the horizon

Andoni Iraola is preparing to take charge of Liverpool for the very first time at Anfield. And fans have been buoyed by the impending arrival of a new signing.

The Reds had barely dipped their toes into the transfer waters before this weekend. Only Victor Munoz had been signed, with Jeremy Jacquet also joining up with the squad after his transfer was completed in January.

But on Friday evening, news broke that Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo will sign for Liverpool on an initial one-year loan deal, with a reported purchase option. Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Savvy transfer masterstroke as move confirmed and next target lined up

Manchester United have less than two weeks to go before their Premier League opener and their transfer business could soon kick back into life

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will hope to make further additions to his squad (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Less than two weeks remain before Manchester United begin their 2026/27 Premier League campaign. Michael Carrick has already added to his squad but further business is expected.

‌



Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow all arrived in mid-July, with a number of youngsters following. Most recently, Colombian midfielder Cristian Orozco arrived from Fortaleza in his homeland.

‌



United have also brought in £38million for Rasmus Hojlund, with the striker completing a permanent move to Napoli. The Dane is one of a number of senior figures to depart, along with the likes of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho.

‌



There looks to be more to come, though, including a newly agreed deal which shows how United's business has changed. Here are our latest lines from Old Trafford.

United are running out of time to decide on whether to meet Bologna's asking price for Jhon Lucumi. The Colombian defender is expected to command a fee in the region of £21m and has no shortage of suitors.

Lucumi, a centre-back, is also wanted by Juventus. However, reports in Italy suggest United or Premier League rivals Chelsea could steal a march by agreeing a sum Juve have so far been reluctant to pay.

Sports.title: FIFA issues furious response on bid to 'undermine' Gianni Infantino after UEFA admission
Sports.content:
FIFA issues furious response on bid to 'undermine' Gianni Infantino after UEFA admission

UEFA confirmed on Saturday a "departure payment" was made to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with FIFA president Gianni Infantino during his time as UEFA general secretary.

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino was UEFA general secretary between 2009 and 2016 (Image: John Walton/PA)

FIFA has lashed out at "a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine" the governing body and president Gianni Infantino following allegations concerning his behaviour at UEFA.

‌



UEFA confirmed on Saturday that a "departure payment" was made to a female employee who was allegedly in a relationship with Infantino during his tenure as the European organisation's general secretary - an allegation Infantino denies.

‌



It was reported that the woman received a six-figure settlement and UEFA confirmed a payment was made alongside covering the costs for an MBA course, stating it was "in line" with regulations at the time.

‌



The allegations pile further pressure on Infantino, who spent 16 years at UEFA and served as its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his failed attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

While not directly addressing UEFA's statement, FIFA accused Infantino's detractors of attempting to diminish his authority and force him from his position without a proper re-election process.

A lengthy statement said: "It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president.

‌



"Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

View 2 Images FIFA's management board backed Infantino at a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday (Image: Sam Corum/PA)

‌



"The FIFA president has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football.

"Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA's president or the institution he was elected to lead.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

‌



"FIFA's responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIFA president and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it."

Infantino's controversial proposal was rejected by UEFA and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino received the backing of FIFA's management board following a meeting held in Morocco, and issued an apology over the manner in which the process was handled.

UEFA's threat to have its 55 member nations boycott FIFA competitions until the plan was abandoned remains firmly in place, with the European confederation stating on Thursday that Wednesday's announcement "changes nothing".

‌



Following the Daily Telegraph's claims on Friday, a FIFA spokesperson was reported to have told the newspaper that Infantino "strongly denies these categorically untrue allegations".

A UEFA spokesperson said: "We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.

"The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

Article continues below

"Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations - which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level - reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo responds as another bride mobbed on his 'wedding day'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo responds as another bride mobbed on his 'wedding day'

Cristiano Ronaldo was rumoured to be marrying Georgina Rodriguez at Funchal Cathedral in Madeira, Portugal, this weekend - but fans actually mobbed another couple's nuptials

View 5 Images Cristiano Ronaldo shared his reaction on Instagram (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has shared his reaction after fans mobbed a couple on their wedding day, mistakenly believing they were the Portuguese footballer and his fiancée Georgina Rodriguez.

‌



CR7, who plays as a forward for and captains the Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr and the Portugal national team, was rumoured to be marrying his partner of 10 years at Funchal Cathedral in his hometown of Madeira this weekend. The famous couple, who have been together since meeting at a Madrid Gucci store in 2016, officially announced their engagement in August 2025.

‌



The pair haven't shared any details of their nuptials so far, but it was claimed that they would tie the knot at Funchal Cathedral before celebrating with their loved ones at five-star Savoy Palace hotel in Funchal this weekend. However, the rumours were debunked after fans accidentally mobbed a local couple's wedding.

‌



5 View 5 Images Fans mobbed a couple's wedding in Madeira (Image: Facebook) 5 View 5 Images The crowd hoped to get a glimpse of Cristiano - but it wasn't his wedding (Image: Facebook)

Over 2,000 football fans and onlookers swarmed the church steps in hopes of catching a glimpse of the superstar couple today. When a luxury grey Rolls-Royce arrived, the crowd mobbed the vehicle assuming the woman inside was Georgina.

But the mix-up was soon revealed as the bride was not Georgina, but it turned out to be a local woman, Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira, marrying her partner Fabio Ramos. The couple, who live in France, returned to their homeland to get married. They have no connection to Cristiano and Georgina.

‌



This afternoon, local newspaper Jornal da Madeira posted footage of large crowds - including people wearing Ronaldo t-shirts - gathering outside the church. The newspaper wrote in the caption that many people gathered, thinking they would attend the footballer's wedding.

Cristiano, 41, couldn't help but react to the footage, commenting on the Instagram post with five laughing emojis. In a follow-up post, the newspaper wrote that Cristiano "was not indifferent" as he showed he was aware of the speculation surrounding his wedding.

‌



View 5 Images The football star laughed at the news (Image: Instagram)

According to reports, wedding guests attending Fabio and Fatima's ceremony had to fight their way through the crowd as fans were convinced Cristiano was the groom. One of the guests said: "Fabio is not Cristiano Ronaldo. This is all crazy. We did not expect anything like this. I don't think he is going to forget his wedding."

Father Marcos Gonçalves, the parish priest of the cathedral, said: "I can tell you that they are nothing to do with Cristiano Ronaldo. This is the only wedding taking place here today." The priest added he didn't believe Cristiano had booked the venue for a wedding any time soon.

‌



View 5 Images There were rumours that Cristiano would marry Georgina Rodriguez this weekend (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

After the couple got married, Funchal Cathedral shared a photo of the newlyweds on Facebook, writing: "We never saw anything like this here at the cathedral. It was very complicated for the bride to enter the church to get married.

"Congratulations to the couple Nicole and Fabio. After a lot of confusion on the street with so many journalists and tourists, we finally managed to close the church and celebrate."

Sports.title: Anthony Elanga horror challenge sparks mass brawl as Newcastle star stretchered off
Sports.content:
Anthony Elanga horror challenge sparks mass brawl as Newcastle star stretchered off

Newcastle United's Anthony Elanga suffered a shin injury after a challenge from Valencia's Jose Gaya

View 2 Images Players of Newcastle United clash with players of Valencia after Anthony Elanga's injury (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Newcastle United’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, rushed onto the pitch to protect Anthony Elanga after the forward was on the receiving end of a strong tackle from Valencia defender Jose Gaya.

‌



The Magpies were taking on the La Liga outfit in a pre-season friendly on Saturday night at the Mestalla as they continued their preparations for the new Premier League campaign.

‌



Jaissle was taking charge of Newcastle for the first time since taking charge of the club and replacing Eddie Howe, and was seen trying to protect Elanga after the Sweden international was on the floor after being tackled by Gaya.

‌



Elanga was stretchered off the pitch in pain, but it’s believed that the Newcastle star is okay and was walking around the dressing room after receiving treatment.

Michael Carrick delivers Mason Mount injury update after cruel blow vs PSG READ MORE :

The former Manchester United forward is believed to have suffered a contusion to the shin, but is thought to have avoided a serious injury.

Following the tackle, Gaya was shown a red card by referee Jose Martinez and the challenge led to a 25-man brawl.

‌



Jaissle and his entire backroom staff rushed onto the pitch as Elanga lay injured on the turf following the tackle. Martinez took just three seconds to issue the red card to Gaya.

Newcastle were forced to substitute Elanga, with Jacob Murphy immediately introduced as his replacement, while Valencia were forced to continue a man down.

View 2 Images Anthony Elanga of Newcastle United is stretchered off after getting injured during the pre-season friendly with Valencia (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

‌

Gaya's two-footed tackle sent Elanga airborne before he suffered a nasty landing, triggering fury from his Newcastle teammates.

William Osula was amongst the first to reach Elanga to assess his condition, with an immediate call made to substitute him.

‌



The full extent of Elanga's injury remains unclear as he departed clutching his knee in distress, a significant setback for Newcastle considering his performance during the first half.

Elanga had a goal ruled out for a marginal offside decision in then first half and put in an impressive performance before the injury.

Newcastle then made four further substitutions at half-time as Aladji Bamba, Osula, Harvey Barnes and Leo Shahar were withdrawn.

Sports.title: Thorslund ends Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again
Sports.content:
Dina Thorslund is a world champion again after ending Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to cap an emotional return to the sport.

Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

The Belarusian broke early in the opening set ​before Alexandrova rallied to force a tie-break, ⁠which the Russian won to ⁠move ahead.

Sabalenka responded by seizing control of the second set with a break for a ‌4-3 lead before serving out to level the match.

Alexandrova held her nerve in the decider as Sabalenka's error count rose. ‌Serving to stay in the match at 4-5, the top seed saved two match points, but a double fault on the third handed victory to the Russian.

"I just tried to play ⁠every single point as if it was ​the last one because with her, you don't [get] ​a lot of chances during the match," Alexandrova ​said in her on-court interview.

"Honestly, I was trying not ⁠to think about the score or anything. Just hit the ball, and that's it.

"I'm super happy that I could win because ⁠after the second set, I thought [the ​chance] was already past me."

Sports.title: McKenna vows middleweight domination as heir to Golovkin and Canelo
Sports.content:
New world champion Aaron McKenna is just getting started.

He secured the IBF middleweight title with a victory over Etinosa Oliha on memorable night at the 3Arena in Dublin.

Now he wants to take on the mantle of Canelo Alvarez and Gennadiy Golovkin by dominating the middleweight division.

He is targeting other champions. Denzel Bentley holds the WBO title, Carlos Adames the WBC and Erislandy Lara the WBA. McKenna is calling for all the top 160-pounders to fight one another.

"It doesn't matter [who's next], whoever wants it. I'm easy to find now, I have a belt. There's no hiding any more. I want to collect every single belt in boxing. I'm the best middleweight and super-middleweight in the world. I don't mind jumping up," he told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive the heart-warming moment that saw Stevie McKenna watch his brother Aaron win the IBF world middleweight title

"I've been thinking about this moment since I was six years old. It just goes to show, don't give up, always stay true to yourself. You can do anything."

His ambitions extend far. "The middleweight division's there to be took over. It's been dying for years since GGG (Golovkin) and Canelo left it. I said it again, a year ago, I think I'm going to be the man to take it over," McKenna declared at his post-fight press conference.

"No one really believed me. Until you put in performances like that and then they start listening. In life you've got to prove yourself sometimes. Tonight I've done that. I just hope one of the other world champions will take on the fight so we can clean up this mess of a division."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title fight against Etinosa Oliha

He promises he will not shy away from any challenge.

"Anyone. I've said it before and I'll say it again I will literally fight anyone out there. I just want to unify, whatever it takes, prove I'm the best in the world. That's the sport of boxing. You look back in the day, the 80s and 90s, they all fought each other," McKenna said.

"And this is exactly why Zuffa Boxing's going to be the future. It's already taking over. Everybody's fighting each other, there's no more hiding."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna had an incredible entrance ahead of his fight with Oliha, first coming into Sinead O'Connor's The Foggy Dew and then Faithless' Insomnia!

For the time being, he can enjoy his accomplishment.

"Twenty-one years in the making," he concluded. "I don't know how long this is going to take for this to seep in that this has finally happened that I've become world champion. I've been dreaming of this.

"For it to happen now, honestly it's literally unbelievable. I can't describe it."

Sports.title: Wissa double gives Newcastle boss Jaissle winning start at 10-man Valencia
Sports.content:
Substitute Yoane Wissa scored twice to give Matthias Jaissle a winning start as Newcastle boss with a 2-1 comeback pre-season win at 10-man Valencia.

But the friendly at the Mestalla threatened to be overshadowed by Jose Gaya's red-card horror tackle on Anthony Elanga, which saw the Newcastle winger stretchered off in the first half and led to both sets of players clashing.

Fortunately for the Sweden international, his injury does not appear to be serious, with Elanga later up and walking after a contusion to the shin.



Image: Tempers flared after Jose Gaya's challenge saw Anthony Elanga stretchered off

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Jaissle was "relaxed" over Elanga's injury.

The German said: "It seems to be not bad, so we are pleased. I hope it's true, then he can start again next week."

He added: "Of course I was in fear [it was a serious injury], definitely, but now I'm more relaxed as the medical department is showing almost green lights, and there's nothing serious."

Who played for Newcastle? Hornicek; Shahar (M Miley 46), Thiaw (Johnson 72), Botman, Pivas (Charlton 67); Bamba (Steur 46), Ramsey (Joelinton 67); Elanga (J Murphy 39), Woltemade (Willock 67), Barnes (Toure 46); Osula (Wissa 46).

Unused subs: Gillespie, Harris, Finneran, Neave.

Elanga's injury after Valencia's Filip Ugrinic's stunning fifth-minute opener had given Jaissle a nightmare start to life in the Newcastle dugout.

But his half-time changes sparked a Toon turnaround with new signings Bazoumana Toure and Sean Steur impressing.

It was last summer's signing Wissa who pounced on a mistake to level in the 52nd minute.

New arrival Toure then broke clear of the Valencia defence to unselfishly set up Wissa for a tap-in to complete the comeback in the 76th minute.

Toure should have had a second assist after fine work down the left, but Jacob Murphy put over his cross in stoppage time.

The win brings some relief to Newcastle on the day they lost their captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

Jaissle's next pre-season test will come on Wednesday as his new side face Everton at Murrayfield in Edinburgh.

Image: Newcastle's Nick Woltemade (left) started at the Mestalla

Wissa's fresh start under Jaissle

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie at the Mestalla:

"A good end to a positive week in Spain for Newcastle - and a trophy for Jaissle in his first match in charge as they lift the 'Orange Cup'.

"Some impressive signs from new signings Aladji Bamba, Steur and Toure.

"Newcastle's travelling fans sent home from The Mestalla with a spring in their step.

"One major positive was Wissa's performance.

"Newcastle really need him to come good this season. It was a huge £55m outlay on a 29-year-old, and last season was a nightmare for him.

"He looks sharp and is coming off a good World Cup showing. Maybe this could be a fresh start for the striker."

Jaissle keeping 'balanced' after debut win

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle speaking at his post-match press conference:

"First of all, I'm really happy that there are no serious injuries. Anthony, we are happy, and it seems to be okay, actually - that was the most important thing.

"Of course, winning games always helps to gain confidence, but we also knew that we had a hard week behind us. The players did well in the camp; there was a pure commitment in each session.

"We had a hard load, so therefore now we deserve two days off, and then we start again.

"It was a friendly today; we will not smash the locker room now and celebrate a lot.

"We're quite balanced; we know what it is about. Now it's pre-season, and we're still looking to work on it.

"It's just a journey; we don't want to hang onto that.

"The victory is higher than it is, but also we don't see the losses lower than it is then, so we should be quite balanced in our approach.

"We should just analyse the situation and develop from there, and that's what we're going to do.

"Now next week, there are things we need to work on, definitely."
