Sports.title: Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha in talks over return to the Premier League after Tottenham exit

Aston Villa are in talks over a deal for Joao Palhinha, their director of football has confirmed.

The midfielder is one of three players that Bayern Munich are willing to sell this summer.

2 Palhinha could be set for another season in the Premier League at a new club Credit: Getty

Palhinha joined Bayern from Fulham in 2024 and he spent last season on loan at Tottenham Hotspur.

His move to north London included a £26million option to buy, but it expired and he has returned to Germany.

With the Portuguese international not in Bayern's plans, he looks set to leave just two seasons after he signed.

A return to the Premier League appears to be on the cards as Damian Vidagany told BILD that Villa are working on a move.

"We need a midfielder because Amadou Onana is out for the entire season - Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans," Vidagany said.

"We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. I believe Aston Villa would be a great club for him."

That was as much as Vidagany was willing to give away, as he refused to comment on further details due to the 'great respect' all at Villa have for Bayern.

Palhinha has made 101 appearances in the Premier League across his stints at Fulham and Spurs.

A move to Villa would present him with an opportunity to play in the Champions League during the new season.

Newcastle United, who have lost Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, have also been linked with Palhinha.

Midfield moves

2 Palhinha impressed at Spurs, but they chose not to pursue a permanent deal Credit: Getty

Villa have already completed two signings in central midfield so far this summer.

Johan Manzambi was brought in from SC Freiburg in a £52million deal that made him their club-record signing.

Villa have also signed Joao Gomes from West Midlands rivals Wolves for £35m.

Ross Barkley, John McGinn, Boubacar Kamara and Lamare Bogarde are listed as central midfielders on Villa's website.

However, Youri Tielemans has departed for Manchester United, whilst Enzo Barrenechea is back at Benfica after a loan spell.

Villa begin their season on Wednesday night when they take on Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup, live on talkSPORT.

Their first Premier League fixture comes four days later on August 23 with a trip to Brighton.

Sports.title: New EFL signing immediately forced to clarify ‘stepping stone’ comment amid backlash
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough signing Radek Vitek has been forced to explain a comment made during his first interview after his transfer.

Vitek signed for Boro from Manchester United on Saturday, but he said that the move was a 'new stepping stone' for him.

2 New Middlesbrough goalkeeper Vitek received backlash for his first interview Credit: Getty

His wording led to some backlash from fans online, as they questioned his mentality regarding the switch.

Typically, the phrase 'a stepping stone' relates to a player using a smaller club solely as a route to join a bigger team in the future, rather than planning to stay for a long time.

After Middlesbrough posted a video of Vitek's first interview as their new signing, supporters flooded the replies.

One Boro supporter replied on X: "Don’t love how he has just called us a stepping stone."

Another questioned: "Did he just say stepping stone..."

"Lad really said ‘new stepping stone’ Jesus. Welcome to the club, I guess," a third Boro fan posted.

But some fans jumped to Vitek's defence and pointed out a language barrier that could have impacted the Czech star.

"I think he means 'next step in my career' having listened to it a few times," another Middlesbrough supporter said. "Easy to mix up sayings when it's someone's second language."

'Not meant in any negative way'

And just a few hours after Vitek's first interview was posted and he faced some backlash, he spoke out on the matter.

"I wanted to clarify what I meant by 'stepping stone'," the goalkeeper wrote, explaining his words on his X account.

What did Radek Vitek say in his interview? In the video posted by Middlesbrough on Saturday, Vitek could be heard saying: "A new challenge for me. "A new stepping stone in my career, a permanent move. "So I'm really excited. I hope everyone is as excited as me for the season ahead and I hope we can go for the goal we all want."

"I just want to assure everyone that I have not meant that in any negative way.

"The point of this comment was that this is a very important step in my career going forward.

"I can’t wait to get started."

Off to a controversial start

Vitek won't have wanted any controversy to begin his time as a Middlesbrough player, but he has now cleared things up.

The 22-year-old has joined the club from Man United after spending the last six years with the Red Devils.

He spent last season on loan at Bristol City in the Championship, following other loans in the EFL and Austria.

2 Vitek spent pre-season with Man United after a loan at Bristol City last term Credit: Getty

Vitek was named Bristol City's Player of the Year after an impressive campaign - and now he's back in the second tier.

Away from his 'stepping stone' comments in his first interview as a Boro player, he also said: “It feels great to be here.

“This is a new challenge for me and I’m really excited to be a Boro player.

“The project here is very impressive, because you can clearly see the ambition and where the club wants to go.

“I’m delighted to now be part of that.”

Sports.title: South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations
Sports.content:
South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations

South Korea’s FA has issued an apology following reports that it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees.

The country’s broadcaster JTBC reported earlier this week that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had offered the services to officials that were in the country for international matches.

3 The South Korean FA is under the microscope yet again Credit: AFP

The allegations date back more than a decade ago with referees offered services on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012.

It is alleged that further indiscretions occurred prior to qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

In a statement, the KFA profusely apologised for the details of the report.

KFA's statement on shock allegations

It read: “We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of.'”

The news report published on Thursday revealed how a sports ministry investigation back in 2016 found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees.

It claimed that it happened on seven separate occasions between March 2011 and March 2012.

The services included trips to massage parlours with the fees inclusive of the costs of sexual services.

“The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,” the KFA added in its statement.

The allegations come after a period of instability on and off the pitch in South Korean football.

A review into an issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo is ongoing.

3 Hong Myung-bo's appointment as South Korea head coach is under investigation

Seoul police raided the KFA’s offices on Thursday as part of their inquiries into Hong’s selection.

The investigation began shortly after Hong’s appointment but to a halt this summer after nearly two years without answers.

However, public anger surrounding South Korea’s disappointing World Cup group-stage exit brought about renewed attention.

Ex-KFA technical director Lee Lim-saeng is accused of offering Hong the job at a bakery near the coach’s home.

South Korea’s sports ministry said in 2024 that Lee’s meeting with Hong was not a formal interview and that the KFA had breached its own hiring rules.

However, the ministry found no evidence of foul play.

3 South Korea endured a hugely disappointing World Cup campaign this summer Credit: AFP

“When I received the offer, I thought they had all taken the proper steps,” Hong said at the parliamentary hearing.

“People may think things were not so transparent, but I never once asked for any special treatment.”

Sports.title: Tottenham star Jan Paul van Hecke hits out at Getafe's dirty tactics - and claims Spaniards could have had THREE red cards - in fiery training ground friendly
Sports.content:
An angered Jan Paul van Hecke hit out at Getafe's dirty tactics after Tottenham's clash with the Spanish side descended into a bruising affair.

Getafe are renowned for their rough-house approach and showed little sign of abating during the 70-minute encounter, which was played behind closed doors at Tottenham's training ground and proved anything but a routine pre-season friendly.

In one instance, Sandro Tonali, who joined Tottenham for £100million this summer from Newcastle, was left incensed by a challenge from Mario Martin. After Tonali had beaten Martin to the ball and shoved him to the turf, the Spaniard retaliated by leaving a leg in when Tonali attempted to play the ball forward.

Tonali was left furious, chasing after his opponent and grabbing his shoulder to turn him around before pushing him multiple times, including once to the neck.

Several Getafe players rushed towards Tonali and the approaching referee, while Andy Robertson stepped in to shove Kiko Femenia away as he attempted to complain to the official.

Centre-back Van Hecke, who joined Spurs from Brighton in a £52m deal this summer, said: 'Sometimes it's good to have a physical game. I thought today was a bit too much. From their side, sometimes it's not necessary, especially in a friendly.

'I think in a normal game maybe they have two or three red cards. But that's also maybe the way they play. We knew beforehand they can do it.

'It's a friendly, so you think maybe they would do it a bit less. But on the other hand, we also need to be at our best because if you don't put your foot in, they're going to win it.

🎥 Sandro Tonali scuffle in pre-season 🇮🇹 pic.twitter.com/XTGblesDyj — The Spurs Watch (@TheSpursWatch) August 8, 2026

Tonali was left incensed by a challenge from Getafe's Mario Martin, rushing up behind him and shoving him several times, including once to the neck

Several Getafe players rushed towards Tonali and the approaching referee after the incident

'If that's what the game asks, then you need to put your foot in and battle with them, otherwise they win the battles. That's what you don't want. It's one of the first things you need to win in football.

'You saw at times it got a bit heated, but that's because of the reactions. If you get kicked, you're going to react.'

As for the match itself, the goals were reserved for the final few minutes worth of action.

Getafe took the lead in the 66th minute when Alberto Risco volleyed past Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky.

Spurs then responded moments later with Conor Gallagher's neat finish following a good run drawing the game in the final minute.

The home side came close to clinching the match late on, with Richarlison's header saved by Getafe goalkeeper David Soria.

Both sides had chances in a goalless first half with Lucas Bergvall's shot the best of the efforts for Spurs, while Andy Gray did well to block Ebrahima Drammeh's drive.

De Zerbi made no changes through the 70 minutes played with barely a break at half time, with lots of senior players involved in another training game played at the training ground on Saturday. Six young subs were named plus goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario. None were used.

Among those not involved against Getafe who are firmly back in the swing of preseason were Martin Dubravka, Kevin Danso, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pape Matar Sarr, Mateus Fernandes, James Maddison and Dominic Solanke.

Tottenham conclude their pre-season fixtures with a double header against Bundesliga side Hoffenheim next Saturday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (3pm UK) and a Sunday match at the training ground (12pm).

They begin their Premier League campaign against Brentford on 22 August.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho lays into Bernardo Silva's fitness after Real Madrid debut - as he highlights how Man City legend 'doesn't do any work' while on holiday
Sports.content:
Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has already hit out at Bernardo Silva after his debut for the club.

Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu earlier this summer, 13 years after his first spell, and one of his first targets was Man City legend Bernardo Silva.

The Portuguese midfielder was strongly linked with Barcelona and Atletico Madrid, but Real won the race and Mourinho wanted his captaincy experience and influence to help improve standards and behaviour in the dressing room following a trophyless season that spawned a number of divisive arguments.

After joining up with the squad later due to his participation with Portugal in the World Cup, Silva appeared for the first time in Saturday's pre-season friendly against Ferencvaros, yet Mourinho wasn't happy with what he saw.

'Bernardo Silva?' he said. 'He's a very important player for us. But the poor guy, when he goes on vacation, he likes to disconnect completely, he doesn't do any work.

'So he arrived for pre-season with much lower physical fitness, and he has to improve.'

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho hit out at Bernardo Silva's fitness after his debut for the club

Bernardo featured in Real's 2-1 win over Ferencvaros in pre-season in Budapest on Saturday

Despite his scathing criticism, the legendary Portuguese boss reserved some praise for the midfielder.

'But Bernardo is a wonderful player who gives us excellent build-up with the ball, whether he plays in a deeper position or in midfield (the 6 or 8 position),' he added.

'During the match I saw that he lacks physical strength, so I moved him to the 10 position. He can play there too. He can play in three or four positions.'

Mourinho's side ended up winning the clash 2-1 in what was their fourth pre-season friendly.

They face further matches against Deportivo and Schalke before kicking off the LaLiga season with a trip to Espanyol on August 22.

And Mourinho was happy with where his side were at, although he felt there were still areas for improvement.

He said: 'I liked the first half more. It doesn’t surprise me because we have been working more with those players. We had very good control of the game.

'In the second half, with Vini and Bernardo, who don’t have many minutes, and with Endrick changing positions, we lost some of our organisation. But it’s good.

'You don’t finish the game by giving away a dangerous free kick like we did. You have to know what to do. Those small mistakes that accumulate in these games are good for me.'

Mourinho did praise Bernardo's qualities but added that he has work to do on his fitness

Meanwhile, when departing City at the end of last season, an emotional Silva, who played 460 times for the club and broke down in tears on his final appearance, hailed his 'unbelievable' journey over nine years.

He said: 'It’s difficult because nine years, it’s a very long time. I would say that I leave as a Man City supporter.

'When I arrived from Portugal, I was a fan of Benfica, but now I can say that for sure that my feelings toward this club are very, very strong.

'I will be supporting Man City for the rest of my life. I also have the feeling of being grateful to the club, to the people, to what the fans gave me back. It was just unbelievable.'

Sports.title: Lionel Messi lands back in Rosario after father Jorge's death at 68... as Inter Miami teammate pays heartfelt tribute during game
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge.

Messi missed Inter Miami's Leagues Cup clash with Monterrey to fly back to Argentina where, according to reports in South America, the 39-year-old will attend a private memorial service.

Jorge Messi - who also served as his son's agent and business manager - died at the age of 68, two months on from the family revealing he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

He reportedly passed away in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, at around 10pm local time on Friday August 7.

In the absence of their captain, Inter Miami players honored Jorge Messi by wearing black armbands, while fans paused for a moment of silence before kickoff. Earlier on Saturday, the team had posted a tribute which read: 'Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family.'

Against Monterrey, stand-in captain Rodrigo De Paul - Messi's international teammate - scored the opening goal and then pulled off his jersey to reveal another which read: 'Messi 10.' Unfortunately for Inter Miami, Monterrey scored late on to snatch a 2-1 win.

Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge

The soccer legend's father, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

Rodrigo De Paul paid tribute to the Inter Miami captain during Saturday's clash with Monterrey

In the first official statement, Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys wrote in Spanish: 'Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.'

The club continued: 'Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

'His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory. Thank you for teaching him to love these colors.'

Later on Saturday, both Barcelona and the Argentina national team added their own tributes.

'Stay strong, Leo Messi and family. We are with you in this difficult moment. We send you our most heartfelt embrace,' Argentina wrote on X.

A spokesperson for FC Barcelona, meanwhile, said in a statement: 'The President and the Board of Directors of FC Barcelona express their deepest condolences on the passing of Jorge Messi, the father of former Barca player and legend Lionel Messi, and, on behalf of the entire Barca family, extend their condolences to the Messi family.

'FC Barcelona thanks Jorge Messi for his commitment to our Club, for entrusting us with the beginnings and the most glorious years of his son Leo's football career. May he rest in peace.'

Sports.title: 'If we maximise everything, it's achievable': TOM CLEVERLEY on Plymouth's promotion charge, working 14-hour days and asking old friend Michael Carrick for help with signings
Sports.content:
'If we maximise everything, it's achievable': TOM CLEVERLEY on Plymouth's promotion charge, working 14-hour days and asking old friend Michael Carrick for help with signings

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

As a man who sang Stand By Me at his Aston Villa initiation in 2014, Tom Cleverley is grateful that Plymouth Argyle got the message more than a decade on.

He is preparing for a second campaign in charge of a club with which he has hit the depths – they were bottom of League One in late November – and very nearly the heights. That they only missed out on the play-offs in the dying minutes of last season is testament to his inspiration and resilience. That he was still in charge was down to the club's patience.

The target is still promotion this time around, but the Pilgrims' progress won't come easy when their competition includes Leicester City and Sheffield Wednesday. They have already sold star striker Lorent Tolaj for £4million to Bristol City and Cleverley will only get to spend some of that on a replacement.

But Cleverley knows his side can compete with the best in the division. Only Lincoln City had a better record in the third tier since the start of 2026 and the 36-year-old former Manchester United, England and Watford midfielder is more prepared than he was 12 months ago.

'I’ve learned a lot,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'The biggest thing is my knowledge of League One. I researched every player we were playing against but until you’ve experienced the heat of the battle, it’s tough to know how to be at your most effective. You never stop learning. You want to be in the training ground 14 hours a day but you quickly learn that's got a short shelf life.

'I've got to grips with what the league takes. I know the strengths and weaknesses of my players. If we maximise every department of the football club, promotion is achievable.

Tom Cleverley is preparing for his second campaign in charge of Plymouth Argyle

He has struck up a strong relationship with supporters after a fantastic run of form in 2026

'I'm very detailed. Which side you press someone off, to when you’re pressing, are you checking your shoulders? All these things, really tactical. Be detailed to give your players an edge, but don't overload them.

'I wouldn’t pigeonhole myself into one style of tactical identity. I’m someone who believes in getting the best out of the players you’ve got, identifying their strengths and weaknesses, and creating a gameplan.'

Cleverley cites Unai Emery as one manager he admires for his adaptability, detail and record of improving players. In the Football League, when bigger clubs regularly poach players, being able to work with what you've got is vital.

He has also called in a few favours from an old Manchester United team-mate, with whom he won a Premier League title in 2013. Michael Carrick let Plymouth train at United's Carrington base last season before their trip to Stockport County.

'We’ve used Carrington, so I see Jonny Evans and Michael there,' Cleverley says. 'We’re good friends away from football, so we've had real good conversations about potential loans. Every young English coach will be rooting for him this year.'

Cleverley enjoys listening to Oasis, Blossoms and Courteeners, all bands from his old city. He'll certainly need some music for the season ahead, when he will spend more than 12,000 on coach trips with his squad for away days from Devon.

Plymouth were surprisingly strong on the road last campaign. They earned 39 points on their travels (one fewer than when they won the title in 2022-23), winning 12 games.

Typically, they travel the morning before a match and train at a club's facilities nearby, before getting home as late as 4am on the night of the game. Players then get a day and a half off to recuperate.

'I've got to grips with what the league takes. I know the strengths and weaknesses of my players. If we maximise every department of the football club, promotion is achievable'

Cleverley (left) with Michael Carrick (right) in the 2012-13 season, when they won the Premier League together in Sir Alex Ferguson's final season in charge

'You want to be in the training ground 14 hours a day but you quickly learn that's got a short shelf life'

'The travelling isn't mentioned as much internally as it is externally!' says Cleverley. 'We try to recruit the right profile of player and character that doesn’t moan about small things.

'We know what we’re signing up for here. We do have the challenge of miles on the clock. It’s not a negative or an excuse, it’s a challenge, and we come across challenges big or small every day.'

After being the first person in and last person out every day, Cleverley is feeling 'refreshed' after a few weeks back home in Manchester and on holiday in North Wales this summer. He's also been to St George's Park to work on his English Pro Licence.

His more than 400 games as a player and manager have contained immense highs and lows. Roy Hodgson once compared him to Cesc Fabregas and he picked up 13 caps for England. He was also relegated with Watford and was the subject of a fan petition to exclude him from the 2014 World Cup, which hit the then 24-year-old hard.

All of that has given him a certain detachment when it comes to the struggles of football. In the pressure cooker of last October and November, when he looked on the brink of losing his job, Cleverley didn't flinch.

'It wasn’t as difficult as some people might have thought,' he says. I suffered a very difficult time in my playing career when I was 23, 24, that gave you a numbness and a thickness of skin in your life.

'It’s difficult not seeing your team win because you don’t sacrifice your life for poor performances or results. That’s hard. You sacrifice so much to see no outcome. But the abuse, I can take that, I've been in football long enough. I enjoy being the person to give direction out of those moments.'

Cleverley's emotional stability is just as well, because he intends to be in this for the long haul. He has embraced the Plymouth community and sees his job as a project.

Roy Hodgson once compared Cleverley (right) to Cesc Fabregas (centre)

He won 13 caps for England and represented Team GB at the London 2012 Olympics

Cleverley's emotional stability is just as well, because he intends to be in this for the long haul. He has embraced the Plymouth community and sees his job as a project

After arriving in Devon, Daily Mail Sport has learned, he went on a local history tour to understand the city. As we speak, he is celebrating a £65,000 grant from Sky Bet for Plymouth to run a programme helping women through their perimenopause and menopause.

'We’re a club that really does walk the walk when we say we’re a community club and a family club,' he says. 'We have days with open training, Christmas carols, whatever it may be, we try to engage and give back to our loyal supporters.

'I’m certainly passionate, intense, players will call me quite detailed. I want to create an energy within the stadium. That’s a real important connection. I’m excited to be on this journey.'

Tom Cleverley was speaking after Plymouth Argyle received a £65,000 grant from the Sky Bet EFL Building Foundations Fund to launch a new programme supporting women through perimenopause and menopause.

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson is 33 and has suffered countless 'horrible' injuries... but she has no plans to hang up her spikes just yet
Sports.content:
There are two conversations that have kept Katarina Johnson-Thompson from calling it quits. To date, only one of them has taken place.

That was a chat with her boyfriend, Andrew Pozzi. As a former world champion hurdler who recently retired, he offered a view of life beyond the track.

‘From what he tells me, the working world is hard,’ reports Johnson-Thompson. ‘So that’s one reason to put it off a little.’

The other reason is more fundamental and traces to a second conversation. That’s the one that hasn’t happened and pertains to an agreement Johnson-Thompson struck a couple of years ago with her coach, Aston Moore.

A sage man of 70, Moore is the kind of guy whose words are heeded, so when he shared a few prior to the Paris Olympics in 2024, they stuck. Johnson-Thompson laughs at the memory of it.

‘I told Aston I didn’t want to be one of those athletes who goes on too long and people are telling you to pack it in,’ she says. ‘Aston was pretty direct in saying that he will be the first to tell me when it’s time. Thankfully, we don’t seem to be at that stage yet.’

Katarina Johnson-Thompson, now 33, has not intention of retiring from athletics yet as she targets a fifth Olympic Games

Johnson-Thompson is 33 and the context here is obvious, because for all the skills in a heptathlete’s set, extended mileage is not one of them – Jessica Ennis-Hill was 30 when she retired, Denise Lewis was 32, and Johnson-Thompson has more scars than either of them.

‘You should see me on a staircase before I warm up,’ she says. ‘When I trained in France a few years ago, I used to live in a top-floor flat and my calf was a nightmare on those steps. God, it can take a while for me to get going!’

She pulled out of the Glasgow Commonwealth Games with muscular injuries in her right calf, but on Friday and Saturday, she will contest the European Championships in Birmingham. A 12th major medal is the goal and, from there, a fifth tilt at the 2028 Olympics.

‘My mind is on the Europeans — I really think I can make the podium,’ she says. ‘But I want to carry on to the Olympics. I looked it up on ChatGPT to see how many heptathletes have done five Olympics but I don’t think AI is much of an athletics fan — it didn’t have the info but I think five would be a record.’ [Daily Mail Sport checked and it would indeed be a record].

The ‘age thing’ is interesting with any athlete – it is one opponent that can never be outrun or outjumped. But for Johnson-Thompson, the retort is that last year she won a world bronze medal.

‘People often ask about it and I won’t say I like it but I do understand it,’ she says. ‘I noticed how few of the people I came up with are still around each year when they announce the team. My friends are all in jeans now and coaching. When Adam [Gemili] retired this year, I saw a tweet that said it was just me, Lawrence [Okoye, discus thrower] and Eilish McColgan [10,000m] from the London 2012 team and that hit home a bit. That was crazy.

‘But I know I can still compete for medals. I’m also in a really good place mentally, especially compared to some of the conversations we have had!’

Our first interview was 10 years ago and many have followed. After the low point of Tokyo in 2021, when the calf gave way months after she overcame an Achilles rupture, she cried as we went over details. She then shed happier tears during our next chat in Loughborough and spoke about finding contentment.

Johnson-Thompson highlights the World Championship bronze medal she won last year in Tokyo as vindication for continuing to compete

There has been a level of introspection that would perhaps go against the recommendations for elite athletes, but there has been the vindication of major gold medals and an Olympic silver two years ago. With it, the KJT of 33 is less prone to self-torture.

There’s a tattoo on her right arm spelling CTRL. That, too, is complicated. ‘I got it before Paris and it’s for “Control”,’ she says. ‘I’m always trying to control everything, but ultimately it reminds me nothing is ever fully in your control and to just go with it.’

It may not be sufficient for gold at the Europeans – Annik Kalin of Switzerland has been the standout in 2026 and Ireland’s Kate O’Connor is riding the high of Commonwealth gold – but KJT’s ability to claim medals is astonishing.

‘I was speaking with my therapist in 2022,’ she says. ‘This was after the Tokyo Olympics and I had lost a lot of love for the sport.

‘The Olympics were meant to be in 2020 when I was coming off a world championship win, at my peak, and then Covid pushed it back a year and I ended up doing my Achilles eight months out from Tokyo. I got to Tokyo and injured my calf. Horrible.

‘The therapist was like, “Things happen and you’ll always see why”, and I was like, “I will never see a good reason for that to happen”. But I feel it’s given me longevity, because I had to find different ways to get to the top.’

Presumably, that time will have a limit. And when it is reached, a wily old coach will have a word. Evidently, that could still be some way down the line.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino comes out fighting: FIFA hit out at campaign to bring president down following bombshell allegation of his 'affair' with former UEFA staffer
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has launched a two-footed assault on UEFA as he battles to save his FIFA presidency.

UEFA announced on Thursday that they will continue to boycott FIFA competitions if Infantino remains at the top of world football after his scandalous plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes to private investors collapsed.

Meanwhile, Infantino has also faced allegations this week that UEFA made a 'departure payment' to a female employee with whom he is alleged to have been in a relationship with while general secretary of European football’s governing body.

UEFA have confirmed a payment was made, but FIFA labelled the allegation as ‘categorically untrue’.

Another turbulent week in football governance culminated in FIFA slamming Infantino’s critics in a 315-word statement on Saturday evening - accusing both the media and UEFA of a smear campaign against the organisation's chief.

‘Echoing the recent statements of CONMEBOL and CAF, as well as discussions with FIFA Member Associations and Confederations from around the world, FIFA will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the FIFA President that is inconsistent with FIFA’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework,’ the statement read.

‘The FIFA President was democratically elected by FIFA’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

‘It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President.

'Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously,' a statement released by football's governing body read earlier

‘Those who do not have the support of FIFA’s Member Associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA’s established democratic processes.

‘Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its President. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

‘The FIFA President has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football.

‘Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA’s President or the institution he was elected to lead.

‘FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

‘FIFA’s responsibility is to its 211 Member Associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our Member Associations and continuing the work of making football truly global.

‘Through the FIFA President and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it.’

UEFA have become increasingly isolated in their resistance to Infantino, with only CONCACAF - the body for North, Central America and the Caribbean - taking a similar stance to the European governing body. There have been fractures in that opposition, however, with Mexico rallying behind Infantino.

UEFA are the sole continental confederation boycotting FIFA tournaments, which one source described to Daily Mail Sport as ‘the only way to force Infantino out’. But, with the endorsement of Africa, Asia and South America, he can fight on.

As it stands, the FIFA president appears to have enough support to survive a vote of no confidence and secure a fourth term in next March’s election.

Sports.title: Inside Matthias Jaissle's first 72 hours as Newcastle boss: A magician, a new training ground mantra and the banned topic of discussion among Toon bosses - plus insiders reveal how 38-year-old dazzled in job interview
Sports.content:
Inside Matthias Jaissle's first 72 hours as Newcastle boss: A magician, a new training ground mantra and the banned topic of discussion among Toon bosses - plus insiders reveal how 38-year-old dazzled in job interview

In a restaurant in Murcia on Friday night, Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle was struck by two things about the magician entertaining him and his squad.

Firstly, the magic, and a sleight of hand that saw members of his party relieved of expensive watches, much to the amusement of those around them.

But secondly, and perhaps more so, the fact the club had thought to fly in the conjurer from the North East specifically for this introductory, team-bonding evening. The new boss, it is said, paused to appreciate the attention to detail.

Because if Newcastle are to survive this season - note, their relegation odds have been cut to single figures this week - Jaissle will need that same meticulous application in every aspect of his own operation. There is no illusion here, a Premier League rookie has inherited a situation that more experienced managers would have sidestepped.

For once the tapas dishes were cleared and watches returned to their rightful owners, the German would have realised there is no time to waste. A 2-1 friendly win over 10-man Valencia here in Spain may have marked his first game in charge on Saturday night, but in just two weeks’ time Liverpool await at St James’ Park in the Premier League.

Premier League rookie Matthias Jaissle has taken on a sizeable task at Newcastle

The new Toon boss appreciated the attention to detail when the club flew a North East magician to perform tricks at a team-bonding evening in Spain

Already, inside his first 72 hours, Jaissle has lost the club’s captain, Bruno Guimaraes, to Arsenal. Before that, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were sold to balance spending-rules deficits. The five players brought in have never played in the Premier League and four of them are aged 20 or under. There was a concern over goals last season and two of the top scorers, Gordon and Guimaraes, have now gone.

From afar, and even up close, a campaign of struggle appears more likely than not. The fact Eddie Howe stood down after originally deciding to carry on is informative. Not that those who remain on the inside share the view that a traumatic summer will extend into autumn and beyond.

Rather, beneath a Spanish sun this week, there has been optimism. There is now a steadfast belief that a reset was needed, on both the balance sheet and football pitch. Howe himself suspected that a fresh voice would bring more from certain players, and those who have witnessed Jaissle’s early sessions say that much has been evident.

One of the key takeaways has been a rule that, in certain zones of the pitch, only forward passes are allowed. If the ball goes sideways or backwards, Jaissle will stop play and penalise the offending team. Against Valencia, the likes of Sean Steur, in particular, adhered to that instruction. The new Dutch midfielder, 18, plays far older. He looks ready to be a starter but may have to wait. Jaissle wants former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, 31, to anchor his midfield and a deal with Marseille should progress in the coming days.

Howe, of course, also wanted to play front-foot football. Having the tools to do so is a different matter entirely, as the former manager found last season in a world without Alexander Isak. But talk of the club’s past - its glories and its failings - is not being entertained by those who are charged with shaping its future, including sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson.

There is great excitement, internally, at the pace of a front three including Anthony Elanga, William Osula and new signing Bazoumana Toure, the Ivory Coast winger who was electric in the second half here. Like Steur, he looks a real find.

Elanga is one of those of whom big things are expected on the back of a poor debut season and, before being stretchered off after a horror challenge that saw Valencia skipper Gaya red carded, he was the pick for Newcastle. The winger, confirmed Jaissle, has escaped serious injury.

He has laid down the law in training, imposing a rule not to pass the ball sideways or backwards in certain drills

Yoane Wissa scored both goals and there is hope that, free of the knee injury that ruined his first season, he will perform to a level that will come close to justifying last summer’s £55m outlay.

But the X-factor, insist the hierarchy, will be Jaissle. They are unlikely to say anything else about their first appointment, and this honeymoon period is not even a week old. Still, there is absolute conviction among insiders when talking about the 38-year-old. His interview was so compelling, we are told, that senior staff wanted to follow him out of the building and offer him the job on the spot. Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan was among those to speak to Jaissle and he very quickly gave his seal of approval.

There is a feeling among the decision-makers that a young manager with no Premier League baggage or previous domestic allegiances will be afforded patience by supporters. He will no doubt need it. Unless, that is, he really can pull rabbits from hats.

Sports.title: Defiant David Sullivan attends West Ham's Carabao Cup victory over Portsmouth after claiming he was being 'bullied' into not watching it amid sexual misconduct allegations
Sports.content:
David Sullivan emerged to take his seat, cloaked in a thick black bomber jacket. Hardly attire befitting the 28-degree sunshine blazing down on the London Stadium but, as Sullivan has made clear of late, he's not too interested in reading the room.

The stadiums operators told West Ham they didn't want him here because they were worried about fan unrest. The club's own fan advisory board said his presence would cause 'offence and upset'.

Sullivan remains the club's largest shareholder but resigned as co-chair in June amid allegations of sexual misconduct, which he strongly denies, and no longer controls the day-to-day running of the club.

This is, after all, supposed to be the fresh start that West Ham need. It's taken relegation to the Championship and boardroom scandal for them to get it but after years of rotten decline this was, at long last, meant to be it and a gentle stroll into the second round of the Carabao Cup under the afternoon sun should be the ideal way to begin.

Everyone should be talking about how Jarrod Bowen, the loyal captain who stuck with the club, scored one and set up another for Taty Castellanos and showed the kind of quality that will see them as one of the favourites to go back up regardless of how clumsily they played in the first half. Or of the impressive displays of youngsters Lewis Orford and especially Mohamadou Kante in a 3-1 win over Portsmouth.

And yet how can the club make a clean break when the man so many supporters hold responsible for their plight, and against whose ownership they have long protested, was so keen to ignore all that advice.

David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium for West Ham's game with Portsmouth

West Ham came from behind to beat Portsmouth 3-1 in the Carabao Cup first round

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Friday that Sullivan felt he was being 'bullied' by 'keyboard warriors' into staying away. He was concerned about the lack of transfer activity, now that he's no longer the man signing the cheques.

The club have so far turned the loan signing of youngster Keiber Lamadrid permanent and snapped up Joel Veltman, who came on for his debut, on a free from Brighton despite selling Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville for a combined £150million. Why should anyone be able to tell him he can't watch the club he supports?

Not one for reading the room.

Many behind the scenes at West Ham were shocked he planned to attend. Daily Mail Sport knew of one staff member who decided not to come due to the 'circus' of it all.

For Nuno Espirito Santo, at least, it was business as usual. 'We are focused on what happens on the pitch,' he said. 'The noise that comes from outside cannot distract us at all. We are going to find a lot of noise. We focus on the game, do their job, and they did it well.'

The last time Sullivan was here, the final game of the season against Leeds when West Ham's relegation to the Championship was confirmed, he did not stay until the end. Fans pelted him with abuse and he left before full-time.

He made it all the way this time. For all the worries that his attendance might turn the place toxic, he sat there - alongside the vice president of West Ham Women Mickey Cornwell - unperturbed and unpestered. The first boos of the afternoon were not even in his direction but at a hydration break during the first half while the PA system played The Bouncer by Kicks Like a Mule. The burly bloke sat next to Sullivan throughout the game looked like he just might.

If anything, the fans acted as if he wasn't even there. Daily Mail Sport was outside the directors' entrance in September when thousands gathered outside to protest against Sullivan's ownership. Even though his expected attendance had been well-publicised, none bothered this time.

The only chant came on 63 minutes when, coasting at 3-1 up, the fans rose in unison to the chant of: 'Stand up if you hate the board'. Sullivan, to be fair, is not even on it these days. He remains the leading shareholder, although former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley would like to change that.

Sullivan was sat alongside the vice president of West Ham Women, Mickey Cornwell

Sullivan, with Karren Brady in 1993, resigned as West Ham's co-chair in June ahead of the airing of an investigation in which seven women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour

The fans were too busy trying to make that fresh start. Before kick-off, a clock on the big screen displayed a 'countdown to walkout'. It meant the players, of course, but this place has seen more than its fair share of exoduses in recent years.

Not this time. For the first round of the League Cup, the London Stadium was impressively full. Forever Blowing Bubbles echoed so loudly around the place that a West Ham-supporting member of the press pack turned and grinned: 'Not bad for a Championship side'.

In fact, it was the travelling Portsmouth fans who took it upon themselves to make the first move. 'You sold your soul for this s***hole,' erupted from the away end after four minutes.

If there was going to be a moment when it turned foul, it was when Adrian Segecic long-range effort deflected off the perennially unfortunate Max Kilman to give Portsmouth a deserved lead.

Nuno Espirito Santo's side, to their credit, didn't need long to turn it around. Kante produced some marvellous skill down the left before crossing to an unmarked Castellanos for the equaliser before Bowen curled a beauty from outside the box to put West Ham in front.

Sullivan remained in his seat and clapped. He did so again after half-time when Castellanos nodded in Bowen's cross and, once more, at full-time. As the whistle blew, he stood up, grabbed his jacket, and left the room. Regardless of the advice, you suspect he'll be back.

Sports.title: Chelsea flop set for MLS move just two months after Cesc Fabregas punt
Sports.content:
Chelsea flop set for MLS move just two months after Cesc Fabregas punt

Former Chelsea striker Alvaro Morata joined Como on a permanent deal this summer and could join another club before the window closes

View 2 Images Alvaro Morata could be on the move again this summer (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

Former Chelsea striker Alvaro Morata could be on the move this summer, despite only signing for a new club on a permanent basis two months ago. Morata joined Serie A outfit Como back in June, having spent last season on loan from AC Milan.

‌



Morata spent three years at Chelsea from 2017-20, and eventually left Stamford Bridge to join Atletico Madrid on a permanent deal, having spent the previous campaign on loan with the La Liga outfit.

‌



The Spain international went on to join Como, who are managed by former Chelsea star Cesc Fabregas, last season on loan from Milan, which included an obligation for the move to become permanent this summer.

‌



Como confirmed earlier this summer that they had completed the signing of Morata on a permanent basis, and now there are reports that the striker could be heading for the exit door at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium.

The report claims that the United States-based club have set their sights on bringing in a striker this summer, with another former Chelsea star, Romelu Lukaku, also said to have been identified as a potential target.

‌



It has been claimed, though, that Lukaku has a preference to join Fenerbahce rather than move across the Atlantic. As a result, it remains to be seen if Atlanta will push on and try to sign Morata.

Since leaving Chelsea, Morata has had spells at Atletico Madrid, Juventus, Milan, Galatasaray and Como, and it now remains to be seen if the former Blues star will be on the move yet again this summer.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy's caddie has earned astonishing amount of money in 2026 alone
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy's caddie has earned astonishing amount of money in 2026 alone

Rory McIlroy's caddie Harry Diamond has raked in a great deal of money this year despite the Northern Irishman playing a reduced PGA Tour schedule

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy's 2026 success has been good news for his caddie Harry Diamond (Image: Getty)

Golf star Rory McIlroy has been playing a reduced schedule this season. However, he has still brought in a tidy amount in winnings and a good chunk of it has passed down to caddie Harry Diamond.

‌



Diamond, McIlroy's friend and long-term looper, has made more money this year alone than others will bring in across an entire season. Estimates put his 2026 earnings between $750,000 and $850,000 (£557,240 and £631,540).

‌



These figures are based on the standard pay doled out to caddies. Generally speaking, they earn a 10 per cent cut after wins, five per cent when the player they work with bags a top-10 finish and five per cent whenever they make the cut.

‌



Diamond's most lucrative windfall this year came at the Masters. McIlroy successfully defended his title at Augusta National, collecting a record $4.5million (£3.3m) winner's cheque with Diamond scooping $450,000 (£334,000) for his 10 per cent cut.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy shows true colours as he's spotted partying at Ibiza nightclub READ MORE :

That payout alone placed Diamond ahead of numerous PGA Tour professionals for the year. McIlroy added a further $840,000 (£631,000) from the PGA Championship, U.S. Open and The Open, including $637,050 (£473,300) for a T7 showing in the former as Aaron Rai claimed victory.

‌



McIlroy's 2026 campaign also featured a T2 placing at the Genesis Invitational, a T12 at the Memorial and a T7 at the Genesis Scottish Open. However, he won't be in the field for the upcoming FedEx St. Jude Championship.

Even his T46 at The Players, T32 at the U.S. Open, and T40 at The Open contributed to the overall figures. A level-par showing at The Players netted $72,000 (£53,000), whilst a T40 at The Open yielded $69,000 (£51,000) for his smallest payday of the campaign.

As a result, a number of tour pros' earnings for 2026 put them behind Diamond, let alone McIlroy. Haotong Li sits at $741,536, with Keita Nakajima at $740,571, Stefano Mazzoli at $720,000, and Rico Hoey at $718,607.

Article continues below

Diamond isn't leading the way for caddy income, though. World No.1 Scottie Scheffler has accumulated $16.9m (£12.5m) in prize money this campaign, with bagman Ted Scott estimated to have raked in close to $1.4m (£1m) as a result.

The Northern Irishman's background outside golf is reportedly in the hospitality industry. His family has links to pubs, hotels and eateries around Bangor and Belfast and maintained associations with the Marine Hotel and Dukes Hotel.

Today, though, it's Diamond's work with McIlroy which has earned him the big bucks. Despite a reduced schedule, the Masters winner is not anticipated to encounter any PGA penalties for falling short of the minimum tournament requirement.

Sports.title: Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea target who had £87m release clause is now a free agent
Sports.content:
Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea target who had £87m release clause is now a free agent

A striker who was once one of European football's hottest goalscoring properties has seen his stock plummet in recent years

View 2 Images Andrea Belotti has endured a difficult few years (Image: Getty)

At the peak of his powers, Italy international Andrea Belotti was one of the world's most in-demand strikers. These days, though, the former Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea target is available for free.

‌



Belotti was a relatively late bloomer, only making his Serie A debut at the age of 20 with Palermo. He left for Torino in 2015, and it was there that he made a name for himself.

‌



He scored a career-best 26 Serie A goals in 2016/17, narrowly missing out on the Capocannoniere award to Edin Dzeko. He signed a contract extension midway through that season, with Torino including a €100m (£87m) release clause.

‌



That clause was only applicable to clubs outside Italy. However, club president Urbano Cairo publicly admitted his fears that it might not be high enough to stave off Premier League interest, as United, Arsenal and Chelsea, among others, were sniffing around.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club READ MORE :

Jadon Sancho's Man Utd decline and manager trend leaves unwanted star in awkward spot READ MORE :

"When I included a €100million release clause in Belotti's contract somebody thought it was an excessive fee, now they think it's not enough," Cairo told Tuttosport in 2017. "I think nobody will come here to trigger his release clause and it would be better for him to stay for one more season at Torino.

‌



View 2 Images Belotti's Torino form attracted plenty of suitors (Image: Getty)

"I've read he's happy here and I'll need to talk to him. He can still improve, play one more season for us, play the [2018] World Cup and then we'll see."

Belotti scored four times in World Cup qualifying but drew a blank as the Azzurri lost a play-off against Sweden to miss out on the tournament. Torino didn't have to worry about anyone meeting his release clause, though, with the striker himself suggesting he wasn't worth that much.

‌



"To be honest, no [I don't feel I am worth it]," Belotti told Mediaset in April 2017. "But given the way the transfer market has developed, increasingly ridiculous sums are being spent. The cost of players has gone up far too much."

But his focus wasn't dented. He hit double figures in each of his first six Torino seasons and was part of the Italy squad which won Euro 2020. When he left his club in 2022, he did so with exactly 100 league goals under his belt.

Things have been much tougher in the years since. He failed to score a single league goal in his first season at Roma and has just 22 goals across more than 140 games in all competitions for four different clubs in Italy and Portugal.

‌

Now 32, he spent last season at Cagliari but was limited to eight appearances after a serious knee injury. According to reports in Italy, he was poised to rejoin the Sardinian club only to fail a medical.

His international career is very much in the rear-view window, with no caps since June 2022. That £87m release clause feels like a distant memory.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard lambasted 'disastrous' Liverpool transfer and pointed finger of blame at manager
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard lambasted 'disastrous' Liverpool transfer and pointed finger of blame at manager

Steven Gerrard was left devastated when Liverpool cashed in on one of their best-loved players

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard didn't mince his words over a certain Liverpool transfer (Image: Getty)

Liverpool have made a number of questionable transfer decisions over the years, as with more or less any top club. However, one sale was still causing pain to club icon Steven Gerrard years later.

‌



Gerrard played with Xabi Alonso at Anfield for five years, winning the Champions League alongside the Spaniard, who is now Chelsea boss. The pair also starred when Liverpool finished second in the league in 2009 but the former Real Sociedad star was sold to Real Madrid mere months later. Alonso was a popular figure with his team-mates and with Reds fans.

‌



That didn't stop manager Rafa Benitez looking to change up his midfield, though. Benitez explored replacing him with Gareth Barry in 2008, though a deal didn't ultimately materialise. Alas, Real Madrid's £30m bid was accepted in 2009 and Gerrard made it clear he believes the manager was the one to blame for what he considered a huge misstep.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mohamed Salah agrees two-year deal with new club after emotional Liverpool exit READ MORE :

Liverpool could lose TEN players for nothing as they fail to learn their transfer lesson READ MORE :

"It was a disastrous decision to sell Alonso," Gerrard wrote in his 2015 autobiography. "I blame Rafa entirely for the loss of Alonso. It was clear Alonso was royalty after our first training session together and Rafa Benitez, who had been so clever to buy him in the first place, was equally stupid to sell him to Real Madrid five years later."

View 2 Images Gerrard and Alonso thrived together at Anfield (Image: Ian Walton, Getty Images)

‌



In a separate interview with FourFourTwo, the former skipper reflected further on the departure. He said: "Devastated, yeah. Devastated. But there was nothing I could do about it.

"Xabi said a long time ago that he wanted another chapter in his career and finally he got it and his team-mates and the coaches couldn't stand in his way. We just have to say thanks and move forward without him."

‌



While Gerrard may have enjoyed the advantage of hindsight in 2015, there was also resistance to Alonso's departure at the time. Supporters demonstrated their backing after that 2008 exit failed to materialise, with Alonso maintaining he had never wished to leave. Benitez didn't last much longer after the sale.

Alonso's replacement, Alberto Aquilani, started slowly after suffering the effects of injury issues sustained at former club Roma. A seventh-place finish meant the Reds' Champions League-winning boss departed on a low note. It didn't help matters that Alonso was demonstrating what Liverpool were missing, winning silverware at Real Madrid and at his final club, Bayern Munich.

Gerrard also compared Alonso's situation with that of fellow midfielder Javier Mascherano. While the Argentine had been keen to depart, eventually sealing a move to Barcelona in 2010, the situation with his team-mate was an entirely different matter.

Article continues below

"Xabi Alonso could still be playing for Liverpool, six or seven years later, so why should he have left at the age of 27 when he still had almost three years left on his contract?" the former captain wrote in his autobiography.

"Mascherano wanted to go, and he refused to play on until he got his move. [Fernando] Torres came to me to ask for help to leave, and he downed tools until he went to Chelsea. Xabi Alonso never once said to me he wanted a move."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick delivers Mason Mount injury update after cruel blow vs PSG
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick delivers Mason Mount injury update after cruel blow vs PSG

Mason Mount lasted less than 20 minutes in Manchester United's pre-season friendly with Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, pulling up on the pitch in what could be a major injury blow to Michael Carrick

View Image Michael Carrick has given an update on Mason Mount (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was quick to downplay Mason Mount injury concerns following Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday. The Red Devils met the Ligue 1 champions in Gothenburg in a pre-season friendly, eager to pump minutes into the legs of first-team players ahead of the Premier League's return later this month.

‌



While Mount was given the nod to start the encounter by Carrick, the attacking-midfielder lasted less than 20 minutes before he appeared to pull up on the pitch. The 27-year-old was spotted hobbling off the pitch as he was swapped out for Tyler Fletcher, before having a lengthy discussion with medical staff.

‌



Mount then headed down the tunnel for further evaluation, as United fans feared yet another spell on the side-lines for the Englishman, who has been plagued with injury since his arrival from Chelsea in 2023. However, Carrick confirmed in the aftermath of the match that it was just a precautionary measure taken by management.

‌



Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly READ MORE :

He told the media: "He got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him. We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful."

Mount has managed just 54 Premier League appearances from a possible 114 as a result of various issues since his arrival from Stamford Bridge. However, the midfielder will be hoping for a season of plain sailing as united prepare to juggle domestic duties with Champions League football.

The Red Devils have just two pre-season clashes remaining ahead of their Premier League curtain-raiser with a newly-promoted Hull City come August 22. United will next take on Leeds United on Wednesday, August 12 before facing AC Milan three days later.

‌



It has been a fruitful summer at Old Trafford, with United bolstering their engine room in particular following the departure of Casemiro as a free agent.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hails Man Utd quality 'people don't always see' after PSG fightback
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hails Man Utd quality 'people don't always see' after PSG fightback

Michael Carrick watched on as his Manchester United team recovered from conceding early against PSG to register a draw against the European champions

View 2 Images Man Utd secured a credible draw against PSG

Michael Carrick hailed his Manchester United side after their draw with PSG - insisting the players were able to find solutions throughout the game.

‌



The Red Devils took on the back-to-back Champions League winners in Sweden and fell behind inside two minutes despite Luis Enrique leaving out a lot of his frontline players.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo was able to equalise before half-time and it was the Premier League side who finished the stronger and can feel frustrated they didn't secure a statement pre-season victory.

‌



Carrick admits he and his coaching staff don't want to constantly solve problems for the players during the game, instead seeing if they can find the answers whilst on the pitch, which he's adamant will stand them in good stead for the upcoming season.

Mason Mount forced off through injury as Man Utd suffer blow in PSG friendly READ MORE :

Man Utd stars give Michael Carrick food for thought in PSG draw as transfer dilemma grows READ MORE :

He told MUTV: "The things that we were trying to get out of the game, a lot of it was there. It's good sometimes that the boys have to problem solve and find their way a little bit. We don't want to always give them the answers, when we don't have to.

"It prepares them a little bit for the season as well. In that respect, there are a lot of things people don't always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there."

‌



Carrick was able to bring on new signing Youri Tielemans during the second-half. The Belgian made a summer move from Aston Villa whilst fellow new boy Andrey Santos began from the start. Both men are part of the club's recruitment drive to bolster their midfield.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick was full of praise after seeing his side in action (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

The United boss will have breathed a sigh of relief with Mason Mount's premature withdrawal seemingly nothing more than a precautionary measure. The versatile midfielder was forced off in the first-half but was able to walk out of the stadium.

Carrick is preparing to embark on his first full season as the club's manager following a stellar interim spell. He came into the dugout in January and presided over a stellar run of results that saw United rise up to third. Now he's being tasked with repeating that form whilst also having to juggle numerous competitions.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
