However, since competing in the 200m and 400m individual medley carries a non-negligible risk of recurrence, and to safeguard the remainder of the competition, the decision was made not to enter these races," explained team doctor Sebastien Le Garrec.

The four-time Olympic champion injured his adductor during the 200m breaststroke heats at the French championships in June, subsequently withdrawing from the rest of the competition.

He suffered a setback during a training session in Marseille three weeks later.

Earlier this month, he had confirmed his participation in the European championships, though he was doubtful regarding the 400m individual medley.

Ultimately, he decided to withdraw from the shorter distance as well as a precautionary measure.

The withdrawal from his two signature events is a major setback for the 24-year-old, who had made these championships the primary goal of his season.

He had also stated he wanted to break his own world record in the 400m individual medley this season.

"It's something I want to do in the near future, and I imagine doing it in Paris at the European championships would be great," he had said.

World.title: Police officer in Dr Mutiso murder had character issues, colleagues say
World.content:
DCI boss Mohamed Amin displays firearm allegedly used during the murder of Dr Victoria Mutiso. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

The latest revelation by the Director of Criminal Investigation, Mohamed Amin, that police officers were involved in the assassination of city psychiatrists adds to the mud the disciplined force has gotten on them.

Arguably, it is under Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen and Inspector General Douglas Kanja that the police have been implicated in some of the worst crimes.

World.title: Charlene Ruto's Koito lights up Kilgoris
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Ruto, is engaged to Tanzanian entrepreneur Isaiah Yunge.

The drums rolled, traditional songs filled the air and dancers swayed in colourful rhythm as Kilgoris was transformed into a spectacular theatre of love, culture, wealth and political power.

At the expansive Intonna Heritage Farm in Naserian Village, President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Chelagat Ruto, took a major traditional step towards marriage as the First Family hosted her Koito ak Chaik—a colourful Kalenjin engagement and farewell ceremony.

For hours, the skies above Kilgoris were punctuated by helicopters ferrying distinguished guests to the President’s family property, while luxury vehicles streamed through the gates carrying politicians, government officials, business personalities, relatives and friends.

On the ground, the mood was unmistakably festive. Traditional songs echoed across the expansive farm as dancers moved to the rhythm, colourful attire transformed the venue into a sea of elegance and culture, and guests embraced the joy of a ceremony that combined an ancient African tradition with the unmistakable grandeur of Kenya’s First Family.

It was romance wrapped in tradition—and tradition presented on a spectacular scale.

The guest list read almost like a roll call of Kenya’s political establishment. Leaving the Narok delegation was Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who joined Kilgoris MP Julius Sunkuli and former Narok Governor Samuel Tunai in celebrating the First Family on the special occasion.

The ceremony also brought together elected leaders from across Narok County, creating an impressive gathering of the county’s political establishment at the heart of Trans Mara.

From governors and Senators to MPs, the event brought together leaders from across the country. Top government officials and senior executives too came dressed for the ceremony

The fashion became part of the spectacle. Brown, maroon and other earthy tones dominated the scene, blending effortlessly with the traditional African setting. It was a celebration in which political leaders seemed determined to make an entrance as memorable as the occasion itself.

But beyond the political faces and the luxury was the heartbeat of the ceremony—culture. Traditional songs rang across the farm. Dancers moved with energy and precision, their performances adding colour and rhythm to a celebration centred on family and love.

The atmosphere shifted between moments of emotion and bursts of exuberance as relatives, friends and guests celebrated Charlene’s transition into a new stage of life.

The contrast was striking. Modern wealth arrived by helicopter, while ancient traditions were celebrated through song and dance. Luxury vehicles lined up outside as cultural performers entertained guests inside. Political heavyweights mingled with family elders.

Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

And amid the glamour, the central message remained simple: Charlene and her fiancé, Isaiah Yunge, had brought together not just two families but two countries.

Yunge is a Tanzanian technology entrepreneur and digital innovation enthusiast associated with Goodsam Technologies and is a co-founder of Smart Kaya LLC, a smart-home technology venture.

He has been recognised among Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 and received the Queen’s Young Leaders Award in 2018. His interest in technology reportedly began at an early age. At 17, he was selected as a UNICEF Africa Youth Ambassador and participated in international advocacy around children's rights.

He later pursued training in sustainable business models through the Swedish Institute, studied Leading Change at Cambridge University and became an alumnus of the Harvard Ministerial Leadership Program.

For all its glamour, the heart of the celebration remained the centuries-old tradition of Koito. Among the Kalenjin, it is a significant engagement ceremony through which the families of the bride and groom formally meet, bless the relationship, exchange gifts and discuss dowry arrangements.

It is a moment when families begin the process of becoming one. The Chaik aspect gives the occasion an emotional dimension, symbolising the farewell of a daughter as she prepares to leave her parental home and begin a new chapter with her husband. Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

For Charlene, the symbolism was profound. Surrounded by her parents, family, friends and some of the country’s most powerful political figures, she was celebrated not simply as the President’s daughter, but as a daughter taking a traditional step towards marriage.

The songs, dances and blessings gave the occasion an emotional warmth that stood in contrast to the scale of the event.

Yet there was no escaping the extraordinary display of wealth surrounding the celebration. Helicopters arriving overhead. Luxury vehicles streaming through the gates. High-ranking government officials and elected leaders arriving in motorcades. Elegant outfits and carefully coordinated colours.

It was a spectacle that demonstrated the resources, networks and influence available to one of Kenya’s most powerful families. The ceremony was therefore more than a social event.

For Charlene, however, beyond the helicopters, politicians, fashion and cameras was the quiet meaning of the day.

A daughter was being prepared to leave one home and begin another. Two families were being brought together.

Love was at the centre. Culture provided the rhythm. Wealth supplied the grandeur. And political power provided the spectacle.

For one unforgettable Saturday, Charlene Ruto’s Koito turned Kilgoris into a glittering stage where romance, tradition, influence and prosperity met under the Narok sky.

World.title: Police join protest victims' Sh25.75m reparations payout
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prof. Makau Mutua, Chairperson of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations. [File,Standard]

A protest reparations panel has approved compensation for 49 police officers, awarding them Sh25.75 million alongside payments to civilians who suffered human rights violations.

The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations approved seven claims involving severe injuries, 37 for moderate injuries and five for minor injuries, according to an update issued Friday, August 7.

"In acknowledgement of the dedication by our uniformed officers to protecting the public, the Panel has resolved to grant appropriate compensation for the human rights violations they sustained during the period in question," the panel said.

The inclusion of police officers adds a new dimension to a compensation programme created against the backdrop of protests in which police conduct has faced scrutiny.

During protests between June 17 and July 7, 2025, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) recorded 65 deaths, 342 civilian injuries and 171 injuries to police officers.

IPOA said most of the deaths were linked mainly to police actions during crowd-control operations.

The compensation programme grew out of the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO) process, which sought to address political and governance tensions in Kenya.

The government later set aside Sh2 billion for victims of human rights violations linked to protests and other demonstrations between 2017 and 2025.

The panel reported that it has processed 680 claims and disbursed Sh896.1 million in compensation.

The panel listed three phases of payments as Sh448.7 million in the initial phase, Sh225.4 million in the second phase and Sh247.95 million in the third phase.

The latest phase covered 175 civilian victims and included 50 fatalities, 46 severe injuries, 49 moderate injuries, 21 minor injuries and nine economic-loss claims.

The panel reported total payments of Sh222 million for the phase.

However, 472 claims submitted through IPOA and KNCHR remain outstanding because applicants have not provided enough supporting documents.

The panel is working with IPOA regional offices to locate affected victims and their beneficiaries and obtain the documents required to process the claims.

The backlog includes 594 of the 600 economic-loss claims received by the panel. Only four have been processed and compensated.

The panel has also received nine claims under the sexual offences category. Eight have been processed and compensated while one remains pending.

Claims involving enforced disappearances remain under review because the panel says the cases require investigation and verification before they can be approved, referred for further investigation or declared ineligible.

The panel has also reclassified three claims from minor to severe after reviewing medical reports and additional submissions.

It approved above-scale compensation for five victims whose injuries it described as permanent and life-altering and said it would recommend that President Ruto include them in a government-funded lifetime medical scheme.

World.title: EACC arrests Kitui County Chief Officer over Sh17.48m procurement fraud
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors arrested by EACC. [Joh Muia, Standard]

The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has arrested Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors over alleged conflict of interest and procurement irregularities involving Sh17.48 million contracts.

In a statement on Thursday, EACC CEO Abdi Mohamud said investigations found that Kivoto, who served in the Departments of Agriculture & Fisheries and Irrigation, allegedly traded with the county through five proxy companies: Shanel Construction Ltd, ECO Stone Ltd, AZ Links Ltd, DTK Construction Ltd, and 4-Walls Ltd.

The companies were paid a total of Sh14.1 million by the county between the 2018/2019 and 2024/2025 financial years.

EACC further established that three of the directors, Josephine Mwikali Wambua of Shanel Construction, Makoma Wambua of AZ Links and Emmanuel Wambua of ECO Stone are relatives of Kivoto. There were also financial transactions between Kivoto and directors of DTK Construction and 4-Walls.

Following investigations, the file was forwarded to the DPP, who approved charges against nine suspects, including conflict of interest, abuse of office, money laundering, and corrupt procurement.

Those arrested are Gladys Mami Kivoto, Josephine Mwikali Wambua Director, Shanel Construction, Roselyne Kyambi Kilonzi Director, Shanel Construction, Mary Mueni Mbiti Director, DTK Construction & 4-Walls, Jonathan Kivondo Kieti Director, DTK Construction and Onesmus Munyao Nzioka Director, ECO Stone.

EACC directed Makoma Wambua of ECO Stone, Emmanuel Wambua of AZ Links, and Stella Nthenya Kioko of AZ Links who are reportedly in hiding to present themselves at the EACC Lower Eastern Regional Office in Machakos or the nearest EACC office for processing.

The suspects are expected to be arraigned at the Kitui Law Courts.

World.title: High Court orders striking nurses back to work
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Uasin Gishu County nurses strike over delayed payments and unfulfilled Collective Bargaining Agreement [Wycliff Kipsang, Standard]

Nurses across the 47 counties have been ordered to report back to work immediately or face legal action from the counties.

Justice Monica Mbaru of the Employment and Labour Court in Mombasa issued orders temporarily stopping the nationwide nurse strike that commenced on July 29, 2026, and ordered the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives (KNUNM) to direct its members back to work.

Justice Mbaru said on Wednesday that any nurse absent from work without proper and lawful cause shall face disciplinary action.

This is after Mombasa County Government and its Public Service Board successfully enjoined the 46 county governments to make the order national.

“In the interim, the KNUNM (respondent) is hereby restrained from undertaking any industrial action relating to the strike notices dated July 21 and July 29 and shall direct all its members to resume duty forthwith and unconditionally to allow the court to address the claim herein on a priority basis,” said Justice Mbaru.

The judge ordered all county labour officers in the 47 counties to record attendance of nurses who report to work and compile a report in court on September 22, 2026.

“Any member of the KNUNM who will be noted by the County Labour Officer as absent from duty without lawful cause shall allow the counties to issue necessary notice to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken,” said Justice Mbaru.

In their petition certified urgent, Mombasa County claimed that the nurses strike has crippled services in public hospitals across all the 47 counties, thereby placing patients facing emergency and inpatient care at risk.

In Mombasa County, the nurses strike paralysed medical services at all medical facilities, including Coast General Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital, Likoni District Hospital and Shimo La Tewa GK Prison Hospital.

Mombasa County, through its Counsel Murtaza Tajbhai, said that the strike had turned from a labour disagreement to a matter of immense public interest.

Tajbhai said that the nurses’ union proceeded with the said strike despite the Mombasa Public Service Board inviting the KNUNM officials for talks to avert the said strike.

The union had raised concerns over the 2025-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), implementation of the 2017 Return to Work Formula and pension terms for Universal Health Coverage staff care guidelines for nurses and the reinstatement of 46 nurses dismissed in Kisii County.

However, in their petition, Mombasa County said that the said grievances could not be addressed by each county individually.

Mombasa County Service Board Chief Executive Officer Fadhil Maamum told the court in his affidavit that most of the demands required consultation with national institutions like the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, while others cannot be implemented immediately given their significant financial implications.

He said that nurses under Mombasa County have no salary arrears and had met some of the union’s demands through negotiations.

Maamum said that while the nurses’ grievances can be resolved, the patients do not have the luxury of time.

“Nurses are designated essential service providers under the Labour Relations Act and the industrial action was unlawful because the statutory dispute resolution mechanism had not been exhausted," said Maamum.

He said the court's intervention will allow for negotiations and safeguard the constitutional right to healthcare.

However, the Union said that the strike was after failed action by the counties to meet their agreed grievances despite continued negotiations.

The nurses said they will not be reporting to work unless guided by the union.

World.title: NTSA blamed for poor signage, costly penalties
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A temporary speed signage on Likoni Road, Nairobi. [Screengrab]

A growing number of motorists are raising concerns about fines issued by the National Transport and Safety Authority's (NTSA) automated speed camera system, claiming they are being penalised without sufficient warning, transparency, or an opportunity to challenge the alleged offences.

The complaints come after the government rolled out a nationwide network of smart traffic cameras aimed at curbing speeding and reducing road carnage.

The cameras automatically detect speeding vehicles, identify registration numbers and generate instant penalties, with notifications sent to registered vehicle owners via SMS.

While authorities have hailed the technology as a game-changer in road safety, many drivers say the system has become a source of frustration and financial burden.

Some motorists claim they have received multiple speeding fines within a single journey, while others argue they were penalised despite maintaining the posted speed limits.

In some places, motorists argue that most signs are on one side of the road, even though the road is a dual carriageway, making it difficult for most road users.

Several have questioned the accuracy of the cameras, citing cases where they were allegedly fined long after travelling through the affected roads.

The debate has been raging on social media, with the latest complaint being on the speed signage along Likoni Road, Nairobi, where motorists are mandated to drive at 30km/h.

"NTSA can't be the complainant, regulator, enforcer, prosecutor, Jury, judge, and collector all-in-one. They could be chasing internal collection targets, while hurting the common man,"

Others have expressed concern over the placement of some speed cameras, saying they are positioned in areas where speed limit signs are either unclear, obscured or insufficient.

"They fined me near Industrial Park Eastern Bypass where on that entire stretch there is no sign indicating the speed limit. This is a shakedown; someone is minting this money," a user on X lamented.

According to the drivers, this leaves road users vulnerable to inadvertent violations.

"There is no problem with enforcing traffic laws, but motorists deserve clear signage, accurate records and a fair opportunity to dispute fines they believe were issued in error," said one driver who recently received multiple speed notifications along the Northern Bypass.

The automated enforcement system forms part of NTSA's broader road safety reforms under the Minor Traffic Offences Framework, which allows specified offences to be handled administratively instead of through the courts.

NTSA says the initiative is intended to eliminate corruption associated with roadside enforcement, improve compliance with traffic laws and reduce the backlog of traffic cases in courts.

Under the framework, speeding attracts graduated penalties depending on how far a driver exceeds the prescribed limit.

Minor violations may attract warnings or lower fines, while more serious offences carry significantly higher penalties.

The automated fines programme also faced an earlier legal challenge after petitioners argued that motorists were being punished without adequate due process.

The dispute centred on whether automated enforcement infringed constitutional rights to fair administrative action and a fair hearing before penalties are imposed.

Road safety experts, however, maintain that excessive speed remains one of the leading causes of fatal crashes in Kenya and argue that consistent, technology-driven enforcement is more effective than sporadic roadside operations.

They contend that unlike manual enforcement, automated cameras minimise opportunities for bribery and apply traffic laws uniformly to all motorists.

Even so, transport stakeholders are urging NTSA to improve public awareness, ensure speed limit signs are visible and regularly calibrated, and establish an efficient appeals mechanism for motorists who believe they have been wrongly fined.

According to Volume 6 on Traffic Control Facilities and the Traffic Signs Manual, the Ministry of Transport is mandated to ensure the speed limit sign boards are erected above pedestrian footways with a minimum clearance of 2.2m from the bottom of the sign to the pavement.

At the same time, the signs should be placed at an absolute minimum horizontal clearance of 0.5 m from the outer edge of the usable shoulder or carriageway.

World.title: Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia arraigned over alleged inciting remarks
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia arrives at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on August 4, 2026. [Nancy Gitonga, Standard]

Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia was on Tuesday arraigned before the Milimani Law Courts over alleged inciting remarks made during a political rally in Kieni, Nyeri County.

Appearing before Senior Principal Magistrate Teresia Nyangena, Kaguchia was read the charge of offensive conduct by the court clerk but did not respond after his lawyers mounted a spirited constitutional challenge against the charges.

His legal team objected to the manner in which the charges had been framed, arguing they violated several constitutional safeguards and should not proceed.

The courtroom was packed to capacity as a battery of lawyers appeared for the legislator alongside political allies who turned up in solidarity.

Among those present were Nyeri Senator John Methu, Nyeri Woman Representative Jane Njeri Maina and several elected leaders who followed the proceedings from the public gallery.

The defence argued that the charge sheet failed to meet the constitutional threshold set under Article 50(2) which guarantees every accused person the right to be informed of the charge with sufficient detail to answer it.

The charge before you does not disclose an offence under the law and purely an attempt by the state to breach the freedom of expression and limiting the opposition.

Lead defence counsel Kiragu Wathuta and Ndegwa Njiru told the court that the MP's constitutional rights had been violated from the time of his arrest.

The lawyers narrated that on the night of August 2, Kaguchia had appeared on Inooro FM's Kiririmbi programme where public affairs were being discussed between 7 pm. and 9 pm.

According to the lawyer, after the programme ended, staff at the Royal Media Services station allegedly informed the MP that about 30 Subaru vehicles carrying hooded individuals had surrounded the premises looking for him.

"Because of the wave of abductions in this country, I advised him to remain within the Royal Media Services premises. At about 5 a.m., I found him having spent the night on the station's couches waiting for daylight," lawyer told the court.

He said that at around 9 a.m., a senior officer who identified himself as a regional DCI commander arrived with uniformed officers and informed the MP that he was under arrest despite there being no summons or warrant issued against him.

"When we inquired why no summons had been issued as is the normal procedure, the investigating officer told us they were acting on instructions from above," the lawuer submitted.

The lawyer further claimed officers initially indicated Kaguchia would be taken to Kilimani before driving him instead to DCI headquarters, where he said advocates were denied access to their client.

"They told us no counsel would be allowed into the DCI premises. Lawyers were locked out and denied an opportunity to consult with the accused," he said.

According to the defence, lawyers later moved to court and obtained orders from Kiambu High Court granting Kaguchia police bail of Sh100,000.

However, they alleged officers at Kamukunji Police Station refused to process the release despite the cash bail being available.

The lawyer told the court that the Officer Commanding Station allegedly declined to accept the money, saying he had received instructions that the legislator could not be released from the station and should instead deposit the cash bail at Central Police Station.

"The accused is not before this court because of any crime he committed. He is here to demonstrate to the country that it is now a crime to oppose the government," he argued.

Lawyer Wathuta also informed the court that Justice Gregory Mutai had on Tuesday morning in Milimani High Court Human Rights Petition No. E517 of 2026 granted the MP a bond of Sh500,000 and directed police to facilitate his access to legal counsel.

Lawyer Ndegwa Njiru argued that Kaguchia could not be required to plead before first receiving legal advice, citing Article 49(1)(c) of the Constitution, which guarantees every arrested person the right to communicate with and be represented by an advocate.

Njiru further challenged the jurisdiction of the Milimani court, arguing that the alleged offence was said to have occurred in Kieni, Nyeri County, and should therefore be prosecuted before a court with territorial jurisdiction over the alleged incident.

He also argued that the charge under Section 94(1) of the Penal Code was defective because it did not disclose who had allegedly been threatened, abused or insulted.

"The charge sheet merely refers to words allegedly uttered by the accused but fails to demonstrate that they were made in a public place or that they amounted to threatening, abusive or insulting words as required by law," Njiru submitted.

He also questioned the accuracy of the translated charge sheet, telling the court he understood Kikuyu and had noticed discrepancies between the original alleged utterances and the English translation.

Njiru argued that the translation distorted the alleged remarks, particularly the reference to the word "Kasongo", and maintained that the inconsistencies prejudiced the accused's ability to understand the charge.

He further submitted that the offence under Section 94 of the Penal Code is a misdemeanour punishable by a maximum sentence of six months imprisonment or a fine not exceeding Sh5,000.

Njiru argued that under Article 49(2) of the Constitution, Kaguchia ought not to have remained in custody for two nights over such an offence.

The defence also urged the court to order the release of the MP's Samsung A33 mobile phone, arguing that it had no connection to the alleged offence.

The hearing on the preliminary objections is still ongoing before Milimani Law Courts

World.title: Tension at Kamukunji Police Station as leaders demand Kaguchia's release
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mukuruwe-ini MP John Kaguchia at Kamukunji Police Station in Nairobi on August 3, 2026. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Tension is high at Kamukunji Police Station as opposition leaders led by Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia and lawyers demand the immediate release of Mukurweini MP John Kaguchia, claiming police had failed to comply with a High Court order granting him police cash bail.

Kaguchia, who was arrested earlier on Monday over alleged electoral offences and incitement, remained in police custody hours after his lawyers said the court had ordered his release on Sh100,000 police bail.

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua in a post on his Facebook account said that the High Court had issued orders directing the Officer Commanding Station (OCS) at Kamukunji Police Station to release the legislator immediately upon payment of the bail.

Gachagua said that despite the court order having been served, the OCS had not acted and was instead awaiting instructions from his superiors. He warned the officer against disobeying a court order, saying that he could be held personally liable for contempt of court if the directive was ignored.

The former Deputy President further referenced the ongoing murder case involving the former OCS of Central Police Station, urging police officers to uphold the law and avoid carrying out unlawful instructions.

Several Members of Parliament from the Mt Kenya region have camped outside Kamukunji Police Station, insisting they would not leave until Kaguchia is released. The legislators accused police of delaying compliance with the court order and questioned why the MP was still being held despite the court's directive.

The lawmakers that claimed they had been redirected to Central Police Station while seeking information about Kaguchia's detention.

Kaguchia's arrest has sparked political debate, with opposition leaders accusing investigative agencies of selectively enforcing the law against government critics. They argue that other leaders who have previously made controversial public statements have not faced similar action.

World.title: Egypt implements new measures to greatly improve mobile phone user data governance
World.content:
The head of the Communications and Information Technology Committee in the House of Representatives, MP Ahmed Badawy, noted that the issue of mobile phone lines registered in the names of people who do not use them has not been completely resolved, despite its decline in recent years.

During a phone interview with Al-Hayat TV on Saturday, Badawy indicated that new measures are underway to identify these illegal lines and verify user data.

He explained that the problem of large numbers of mobile phone lines being registered in the names of people who do not use them has persisted for years, being particularly significant from 1998 until 2017.

Addressing Illegal Mobile Lines

The head of the Communications Committee pointed out that measures to curb this issue began in 2018, including halting dealings with unauthorized agents and distributors, restricting the sale of mobile lines to company branches, and requiring activation through the call centers of telecommunications companies.

While Badawy confirmed that these measures have contributed to a decline in illegal lines, it has not eradicated the problem completely.

He explained that technological advancements and digital transformation, along with the misuse of phones and the link between some cybercrimes and mobile numbers, have made addressing the issue even more critical.

Badawy revealed new measures to enhance the governance of mobile line user data, including expanding the process of obtaining additional information to verify the line owner’s identity.

He noted that the Communications Committee is monitoring these measures.

How can citizens find out?

Badawy urged citizens to check all mobile phone lines registered in their names, emphasizing that any citizen who discovers a number registered in their name but not in use can take steps to cancel it.

He explained that citizens can check through the “My NTRA” application.

If a number appears registered in their name despite not being used, they can contact their mobile network operator to take the necessary steps and cancel the line.

Badawy confirmed that the four mobile network operators are handling these cases, while the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority is working with the telecommunications service providers to identify lines registered in the names of some individuals but used by others.

Lines used in crime

The head of the House of Representatives’ Communications Committee stressed that registering a phone line in someone’s name does not necessarily mean they committed a crime.

He emphasized that legal responsibility lies with whoever is proven to have committed a crime using the number.

He clarified that not all phone lines registered in names other than their users have been linked to crimes, but anyone proven to have used one of these numbers to commit a crime will be held accountable according to the law.

Fake Accounts

Badawy revealed another aspect of the case, indicating that there are instances of fake social media accounts being created using some of these phone numbers.

He noted that extensive investigations are underway regarding these cases, without disclosing further details, and confirmed that the relevant authorities are continuing to monitor the situation.

World.title: Will fuel prices increase in Egypt anytime soon?
World.content:
The head of the Petroleum Products Division at the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce, Hassan Nasr, said that the local market is operating stably, with fuel available in all governorates.

He noted that petroleum product prices have not seen any new increases so far, while predicting future price trends is difficult due to their dependence on several local and global variables.

During a phone interview with Al-Shams TV on Saturday, Nasr added that petroleum products are readily available in the markets, emphasizing that there is no supply crisis or shortage of fuel for consumers.

He explained that fuel prices are currently linked to a range of economic variables and global market fluctuations, making it impossible to issue accurate price forecasts for the coming period.

Rising Transportation and Insurance Costs

The head of the Petroleum Products Division pointed out that successive geopolitical development are impacting energy markets, especially with the continued tensions in several regions.

He noted that these developments are reflected in the costs of transporting oil and petroleum products, as well as insuring shipments.

He added that maritime transport and insurance costs for ships and vessels in the Arabian Gulf region have increased by between 20 to 25 percent, which is one of the factors included in the cost of transporting and handling petroleum products.

Nasr explained that the price of Brent crude in global markets is one of the main factors affecting petroleum product pricing calculations, along with the exchange rate of the US dollar against the Egyptian pound.

Other influencing factors include inflation rates and transportation and logistics costs, as significant fluctuations in global oil prices or in the exchange market can affect calculations related to setting fuel prices locally, he said.

The Pricing Committee

Nasr emphasized that fuel prices are not determined based on personal expectations or individual estimates, but rather on studies and calculations that include a range of economic and technical indicators, with the participation of relevant authorities and sectors.

He affirmed that the decision to increase or maintain petroleum product prices rests with the competent authorities and the Automatic Pricing Committee, explaining that this matter is subject to monitoring in light of economic changes and global market fluctuations.

Future Fuel Prices

Current circumstances make predicting fuel prices in the coming period extremely difficult, he noted, especially given the rapid changes in oil markets and the political and security developments in the region.

However Nasr assured that the current situation in the Egyptian market is stable and that petroleum products are readily available, emphasizing that no new fuel price increases are planned for the near future.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: The Odyssey surpasses US$1 billion in 3 weeks
World.content:
Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” (2026) surpassed the one billion dollar mark in just three weeks since its release.

The film grossed $ 429.65 million domestically and $ 578.8 million internationally, bringing its total earnings to $1.008 billion.

The Odyssey is Nolan’s first film to cross the billion-dollar threshold since “The Dark Knight Rises” in 2012, which earned $ 1.08 billion.

“The Dark Knight”, released in 2008, also grossed $ 1.008 billion.

The Odyssey is expected to become Nolan’s highest-grossing film in the coming days, surpassing the earnings of both The Dark Knight Rises and The Dark Knight.

This remarkable achievement for a nearly three-hour drama based on the ancient Greek epic poem The Odyssey – dating back almost 3,000 years – solidifies Nolan’s position as one of the most prominent directors capable of achieving widespread popular and commercial success.

IMAX screens accounted for a significant portion of the film’s revenue, generating $ 257 million in total ticket sales: The Odyssey is expected to become the highest-grossing film in the company’s history by the end of its opening weekend.

The film surpassed the billion-dollar mark before its release in China, the world’s second-largest film market, where it is scheduled to premiere on August 14.

It is anticipated to be a massive success, screening on approximately 800 IMAX screens, in addition to thousands of traditional theaters.

The film, written, produced, and directed by Nolan, is a Universal Pictures and Synopsis production.

Matt Damon stars as Odysseus, the king of Ithaca, who embarks on a perilous journey to return home and reunite with his wife after the Trojan War.

The cast also includes Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Lupita Nyong’o, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, and Jon Bernthal.

World.title: Erdogan comments on Mecca Joint Defense Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan affirmed on Friday that the “Mecca Joint Defense Agreement,” signed between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, represents a strategic step to enhance security and defense cooperation among the three countries.

In a post on the X platform, he stressed that this agreement follows the principle of collective deterrence and is not directed against any country.

Erdogan said “Today, I visited Mecca in response to the gracious invitation of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Prime Minister, Prince Mohammed bin Salman.”

He explained: “During the visit, I met with my dear brother, Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. On this occasion, we, as the three countries, signed a joint defense agreement.”

The Turkish President continued: “This agreement is based on the principle of collective deterrence and aims to strengthen security and defense cooperation, develop joint projects in the defense industries, and contribute to the fight against terrorism.”

According to Erdoğan, the agreement affirms the right of legitimate self-defense stipulated in Article 51 of the UN Charter and not directed against any specific country and remains open to the accession of all friendly nations that share the goal of promoting security, prosperity, and stability in the region.

He noted that Turkey, based on desire for regional responsibility, will continue its principled stance advocating for the resolution of conflicts and crises through dialogue and diplomacy, and on the basis of respect for international law.

The Turkish President concluded his statement by saying, “I pray to Allah that this visit, the consultations we held, and the agreement we signed will bring goodness and blessings to our entire region.”

World.title: The EMA reveals new heatwave across Egypt starting Tuesday
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) announced the start of a new heatwave across the country, beginning on Tuesday.

Temperatures will skyrocket, with Cairo experiencing a perceived temperature of 40C during the day, and reaching 45C in Upper Egypt.

The EMA explained that until Thursday, very hot and humid conditions will persist during the day in most parts of the country, with warm and humid weather at night.

It added that maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and the Lower Egypt will reach around 36C on Sunday, rising to 40C on Tuesday and Wednesday, before dropping to 37C on Thursday.

In northern Upper Egypt, maximum temperatures will range between 37-40C, while southern Upper Egypt will experience even higher temperatures, ranging between 40-45C during the forecast period.

This makes southern Upper Egypt one of the regions most affected by the heatwave.

The authority also noted that high humidity levels will increase the perceived temperature in the shade by two to four degrees, making the weather feel hotter than the recorded temperatures.

The EMA warned of fog formation between four to eight am on several roads leading to and from northern Egypt, including Greater Cairo, the Suez Canal cities, central Sinai, and northern Upper Egypt.

The fog may be dense at times on certain roads.

The EMA also predicted occasional wind activity on Sunday along the northern coast and the Western Desert, and on Wednesday and Thursday in southern Sinai and southern Egypt, with intermittent periods of wind.

It recommended following daily bulletins and updates, especially given the continued high humidity levels and their impact on the perceived temperature.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Saudi Arabia turns to Muslim military heavyweights in landmark defense pact as Iran war closes in
World.content:
Saudi Arabia has drawn two of the Muslim world’s most formidable military powers into its defense as the Iran war moves closer to the kingdom.

Pakistan and Turkey signed a NATO-style mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia in Mecca on Friday, consolidating their longstanding security ties into a collective-defense alliance that stipulates an attack against any of them “shall be regarded as attack on them all.”

That commitment could draw Pakistan and Turkey into a war they have carefully kept at arm’s length.

The official rationale for the agreement is “to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression” and further provide “for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation among the three states,” according to a statement released by all three countries.

More specifically, the pact gives Saudi Arabia a powerful new layer of protection beyond its longstanding security partnership with the United States amid growing regional doubts over whether Washington can still be relied upon to protect its oil-rich Gulf allies.

Turkey has the second-largest military in NATO, behind only the US, while Pakistan is the only nuclear-armed Muslim nation.

Such powerful allies strengthen Saudi deterrence and present a united Sunni-led military front against a mounting Iranian threat, though a Turkish official told CNN the agreement isn’t directed against any specific actor and the Saudi foreign ministry insisted this “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc.”

Other regional countries can also join, the Turkish official added, raising the prospect of the alliance drawing in new members much like NATO.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan is received by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, before they signed the pact. Saudi Press Agency/Handout/Reuters

The statement ⁠did not give specifics on the commitments each had accepted, and it is unclear how far the agreement would bind the three countries to any particular military action in each other’s defence.

The pact also comes as Israel expands its military reach across the region and Riyadh’s relations with the neighboring United Arab Emirates fray.

Pakistan and Turkey each share a border with Iran and both have strong reasons to prevent the conflict from spiraling. Pakistan must manage its sizeable Shiite population and its sensitive relationship with Tehran, while Turkey and Iran share concerns over Kurdish separatism despite competing elsewhere in the region.

Tehran repeatedly struck targets in Saudi Arabia during the war, including civilian infrastructure, energy facilities and US interests. Direct Iranian attacks on Saudi Arabia largely subsided after an April 8 ceasefire took hold, but Iran-backed groups in Yemen and Iraq continued targeting the kingdom.

Riyadh has been one of the war’s most vocal opponents and has worked to restrain US President Donald Trump from escalating against the Islamic Republic. Yet the attacks Saudi Arabia continues to face from multiple fronts have left officials increasingly alarmed and frustrated.

Vehicles move along a road as smoke billows from an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia after a reported Iranian drone strike in March. Stringer/Reuters

A Saudi official told CNN on Thursday that the kingdom was bracing for a major, coordinated assault by Iran-backed militias in Iraq and Yemen, supported by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. CNN has also reported that Tehran warned Gulf nations that renewed US attacks would trigger retaliation against energy or desalination facilities across the region.

The treaty signed in Mecca on Friday therefore serves as a warning to Tehran: another major attack on Saudi Arabia could invoke the pact, draw Pakistan and Turkey into the conflict and dramatically widen the war.

Reaction emerging from Tehran indicated their dissatisfaction toward the agreement, as a senior Iranian official warned that it will not guarantee Saudi Arabia’s security.

“The Saudis should understand that a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan will not bring them security, just as decades of one-sided dependence on the Americans failed to do so,” Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, said on X.

The agreement solidifies deepening military ties between these nations. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a formal mutual defense pact last September, even before Iran started directly striking Saudi sites.

World.title: Trump dismisses climate change. But he can’t deny that wildfires are going to get worse
World.content:
Destructive wildfires are part of life in much of the US now, as Americans adapt to the warming planet and its more intense weather starts to feel common.

This summer, Spokane, Washington, most notably saw neighborhoods decimated and tens of thousands face evacuation. But wildfires affected much of the Western US, leveling homes in Utah and Colorado, among other states, to say nothing of the frightening pictures out of Europe and the smoke that has poured into the US from Canada.

President Donald Trump, who has described climate change as a “hoax,” has withdrawn the US from international efforts to address the issue and slashed domestic efforts to counter it, wondered last month if Canada should pay the US damages for smoke that has “poisoned” US air, as if Canada could control either the air flow or the fires any more than the US.

His EPA has all but dismantled an office that was researching the effects of smoke on humans, according to the New York Times.

In recent years, Texas, Tennessee, Florida, California and Hawaii, among other states, have seen homes destroyed and lives uprooted. Fires rage each year in forestland across the West.

Miriam Sim, 76, reacts as she walks through the burned remains of her neighborhood after a wildfire hit the northern part of Spokane, Washington, on Monday, Aug. 3. Lindsey Wasson/AP

It will be harder to assess the cost of these disasters, along with other climate-related weather events, after Trump’s administration stopped tracking them as a result of cuts at NOAA, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — although a nonprofit has tried to fill the void. Wildfires in Los Angeles early in Trump’s second term cost an estimated $63 billion.

Trump has also moved, without approval or funding from Congress, to completely reorganize the sprawling patchwork of agencies that deploy wildland firefighters in US by creating the new US Wildland Firefighting Service. That may be a worthy ultimate goal, but Congress wants him to slow down and study the issue, and has refused to fund the agency as Trump’s administration envisions it.

Those DC disagreements aside, wildfires continue to spread.

I talked to Brandon Miller, CNN’s lead meteorologist and the network’s climate crisis beat leader about this year’s fires, fires in general, what to expect in the future and what communities can do.

Our edited conversation is below.

How does this fire season compare?

WOLF: The big headlines this summer have been from Spokane, Spain, and France. How is this fire season compared to others so far?

MILLER: It’s above average pretty much everywhere we look. We’re about 50% above normal for the amount of area that has burned across the US up to early August. That’s 50% above normal over the last 10 years. The last 10 years has already been above normal.

If you compare that to a couple of decades ago, that’s already increased by probably 50%, just the baseline. So we just continue to march ever upward when it comes to the amount of area burned.

A person rides a personal watercraft on Okanagan Lake, in Lake Country, British Columbia, as the Quilpituk Creek wildfire burns on the mountainside across the lake near Fintry, on August 3. Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press/AP

What’s going on around the world?

WOLF: How do the US fires compare to worldwide fires?

MILLER: It’s certainly not exclusive to the US and it’s even worse in other locations, places like Canada that are above average this year by a good margin and the last four years are each of their top four years as far as burned areas. This is just an annual thing now.

I’ve been covering global weather here at CNN for 20 years, and every year somewhere in Europe is burning, and it’s and it’s more than we’ve seen before. Last year it was Greece and Italy. This year, it’s Spain, it’s France, it’s the UK. Pretty much everywhere in Europe is setting temperature records each summer.

Here in the US right now, Oregon and Washington lead the lead the nation in the number of large fires. California isn’t yet, but there’s plenty of time for that to change. Many years, California and Colorado are leading. The exact locations may change from year to year, but the overall area burns, the overall number of fires, all those things continue to march upwards.

The season is now never-ending

WOLF: Is there something about preparation or preparedness in California that was different this year so far, or have they just been lucky?

MILLER: Not necessarily lucky. Their fire season tends to come later in the year. Into autumn is when they get more of those big windstorms, those Santa Anas that you’ve probably heard of. Strong wind events can really dry out those fuels. They don’t really get rain there over the summer. and so that’s when things really start to dry out. By the time the winds arrive in the fall, that’s when they see a lot of their big fires. Oregon and Washington aren’t typically areas that get as dry and hot. A lot of those places, especially there along the Pacific, don’t even have air conditioning. But when they’re having days and days of 90- and 100-degree temperatures, that’s indicative of something way different than what used to be. When you see those temperature records, it is very likely fire is to follow.

Flames consume vegetation as the Gann Fire burns near Copperopolis, in Calaveras County, California, on Tuesday, Aug. 4. Noah Berger/AP

What can (and can’t) be blamed on climate change

WOLF: The Spokane Fire was allegedly set by an arsonist. If that’s the case, is it appropriate for us to attribute climate change to that in any way?

MILLER: Yes and no. People have always caused fires, whether purposefully or, most of the time, it’s an accident. A campfire could ignite. Starting your car on dry grass can ignite a wildfire. Humans have always caused fires, and the percentage of human versus natural causes hasn’t really changed much in recent years. To say that climate change caused the Spokane fires — no, absolutely that would be an incorrect thing to say.

But did it prime the area to burn in the way that it did? Absolutely.

What’s the recipe for a wildfire in this climate change era?

WOLF: What are the ingredients that make for increased wildfire risk and why are they turbocharged by climate change?

MILLER: It’s not so difficult to think about. The drier something is, the more likely it is to burn. The hotter something is, the drier it gets. Climate change is changing the atmosphere’s thirst. It’s causing evaporation to happen more quickly, and that lowers water levels. In the western reservoirs we’re seeing record lows at Lake Mead and Lake Powell. It also is removing water from trees, from brush, from forests, and that makes them more likely to burn.

The flip side of that is, if everything just got drier and drier continuously, some of these areas would become deserts and after a long time, wouldn’t burn so much.

But the problem is this weather whiplash that we see — and we see this a lot with California, where they’ll go from a really wet year to a really dry year. So you get a really wet year, maybe some of the climate patterns that are naturally occurring, El Niño and La Niña. Ironically, climate change also makes wet patterns wetter because warmer air, as the climate warms, can hold more water in it. So you might get a very lush year that grows a lot of vegetation, and then when the next year comes and it’s the hottest and driest on record, it doesn’t take a degree in climatology to figure out that’s going to be a really bad burn year. That’s what we’re seeing. That’s what’s happened in Europe as well. They had a very wet winter, and this summer has been the hottest on record by a good margin. And so that’s setting the table for a really bad fire situation.

A person stands at an overlook above Lake Mead near Boulder City, Nevada, on July 21, 2026. Caroline Brehman/Reuters

Why wildfires rage in wet places

WOLF: Dryness and fire danger on the West Coast makes sense. But there were fires in Hawaii recently. Earlier this year, there were bad fires in Florida. Is there anywhere that’s immune from this?

MILLER: I wouldn’t say anywhere is immune. Certainly, anywhere that has forests and wildland is subject to those burning. Here in the Southeast, we had Gatlinburg a few years back, where there was really bad fire. That opened a lot of people’s eyes to, this isn’t just a West Coast problem.

The Great Lakes and some of the interior Northeast probably sees the lowest incidents. Florida surprises a lot of people because they get so much rain, but when the rain shuts off, even for just a short amount of time, it’s so hot that things dry out very quickly. They also have the most lightning per square mile of anywhere in the country. Lightning is one of the No. 1 causes of fires. Just a couple weeks of no rain and really hot temperatures followed by a thunderstorm in Florida can ignite dozens of fires.

Desirable living areas can mean more fires

WOLF: What made the Spokane Fire so destructive is that it entered developed communities. That’s happened across the country now. Is there a documented increase in this crossover between wildfires and civilization? What is causing it?

MILLER: It’s actually a very active area of research. It’s known as the “wildland-urban interface,” and there are millions of people in the US alone that live in what would be classified as a wildland-urban interface. As we’ve built out cities, we are infringing upon what was before wildlands or forests. These are desirable places to live. Just like living on the coast, even though it’s very vulnerable to hurricanes, is a desirable place to live for obvious reasons. But what that does is it butts up into nature, and nature naturally burns.

The natural burning process of forests is actually a good thing, which is why we have prescribed burns and things that are designed to make the forest healthy. It keeps the forest healthy and clears it of that growth. The other thing with the wildland urban interface — those forests aren’t necessarily maintained as well as they could have or should have been, because those prescribed burns are burns. They’re fires. People don’t like those fires. They don’t want to have some of their nicest days the summertime full of smoke. Forest management runs against that all the time.

Also, you can’t do a prescribed burn if the conditions are dangerous. They want a day with low fire danger, with a lot of moisture in the forests. But those days, a lot of years, just aren’t very plentiful. So it’s getting harder. Climate change is working against that as well. That may be something governments are going to have to do more of or do differently.

Chimneys are the only structures remaining in a residential neighborhood after a wildfire hit the northern part of Spokane, Washington, on August 3. Lindsey Wasson/AP

What homeowners can do

WOLF: What else do they need to be doing, and what are they doing to address this as in terms of prevention?

MILLER: A lot of that, you know, can be managed on the development side — making houses in a more fire-sustainable way that going to give natural fire breaks. Not having as flammable materials, not having landscaping in your yard that that is vulnerable to fire. There’s a lot of things that homeowners themselves can do, just at an extremely local level to maximize their home or their neighborhood’s chances to survive a fire.

WOLF: What’s a fire break? Not putting houses right next to each other?

MILLER: Don’t put houses right next to that forest, really, is the thing. You want to have that natural break. With the wildland urban interface, they’re trying to figure out exactly how much needs to be there, what they can put in those locations, because once one house burns in a in a neighborhood, if there’s any wind at all, it’s going to go from house to house to house to house very quickly. The wind carries those embers extremely efficiently, and just a couple of those landing on a roof can quickly lead to a house burning.

What climate scientists and firefighters are saying

WOLF: Climate science predicted there would be more and more intense fires. That is happening. What do climate scientists think will happen next?

MILLER: More of this exactly. More of the burned area increasing. It’s because the fire season is increasing. It’s starting earlier and it lasts longer. If you look back at Canada, for instance, it never really started burning there until June or or July, because there was still snow on the ground until quite late. It took months to really dry out and heat up. But now it’s happening on both ends. You get less snow in a lot of years, so it melts quicker, and that exposes that vegetation. It’s growing sooner, and then drying out sooner, and then it’s taking longer for the snow to come back, and the rains and the cooler temperatures. Especially in some of those higher-latitude areas — Canada, Europe, Russia — where we’ve seen the worst and the most fire activity, we do expect that trend to continue.

I’ve talked to a lot of wildland firefighters in recent years, and the one thing they talk about so much — those firefighters tend to be a fairly conservative bunch, not ones that you would typically expect to talk about environmental, climate change, things like that. But they have no doubt, because they’ve seen it in with their own eyes how things have changed, and the thing they point to the most is nighttime recovery.

Nighttime was always their time to fight these fires. Even the most aggressive fires, they might have to come back, retreat a little bit during the day, but at night they would be able to really attack these fires and hopefully get them to a good place ahead of the next day when it would get hot and the winds would pick up in the afternoon. It basically doesn’t happen anymore. Just like the fire season has grown to a fire year, the fire day is now 24 hours. There’s less time or ability to really gain ground on these fires, and that’s why sometimes they can grow so exponentially, even in the overnight hours.

World.title: Iran displays wreckage of downed US and Israeli aircraft
World.content:
Iran is showing off some of the US and Israeli aircraft it has brought down during the almost six-month war in the Persian Gulf.

State-run Press TV posted images on social media Friday of the remnants of a US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet, several drones and what appear to be the engines of an MC-130J Commando special operations aircraft.

“Images of US-Israeli aircraft shot down by the IRGC Aerospace Force’s newly developed air defense system,” a caption reads, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

The F-15 and MC-130 wreckage are likely from the only incident where those two types of aircraft were lost in Iran. On April 3, an F-15 was hit by anti-aircraft fire and its crew of two ejected.

Both service members were eventually recovered by US Special Operations forces — but during the rescue operation, two of the four-engine MC-130s got stuck on a makeshift desert airstrip and had to be destroyed.

As for the drone wreckage on display, reports say the US lost a number of the unmanned aircraft during the war, but the Pentagon has not confirmed any specifics.

The reports from Press TV did not include the location of where wreckage is displayed, but it appears to be in a large underground bunker.

World.title: Liberia: Dismissed LNP Commander Seeks Bail In Liberia’s Biggest Cocaine Case
World.content:
Former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell W. Kwabo Challenges Detention as Court Battle Intensifies in US$317 Million Drug Trafficking Scandal

By: Willie N. Tokpah

Monrovia-Former Liberia National Police Highway Patrol Commander Wadell W. Kwabo, one of the highest-ranking security officials to be criminally charged in Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking investigation, has formally petitioned Criminal Court “C” at the Temple of Justice for bail, arguing that prosecutors have failed to establish sufficient evidence linking him to the multi-million-dollar drug trafficking operation that has shaken the country’s security establishment.

Kwabo, who was dismissed from the Liberia National Police by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai following the findings of a Joint National Security Investigative Task Force, is accused of using official police resources to facilitate the movement of an estimated 4.2 metric tons of cocaine valued at approximately US$317 million.

The case has become one of the most consequential anti-narcotics prosecutions in Liberia’s history, exposing alleged collusion between transnational drug traffickers and senior state security personnel.

Through his lawyers, headed by Cllr. Sayma Syrnius Cephus, Kwabo contends that “proof is not evident and presumption is not great” to justify his continued detention.

The defense argued that prosecutors have failed to produce objective evidence placing him at the crime scene before or during the commission of the alleged offenses and insists that the accusations against him rest primarily on statements made by co-defendant Christian Nyantee, who is allegedly attempting to reduce his own criminal liability by implicating others.

According to the defense motion, Kwabo is being prosecuted largely because investigators alleged that he provided an escort to the principal defendants after the crimes had already been committed.

His lawyers maintained that providing security escort is a routine responsibility of the Highway Patrol Section, particularly during operations involving members of Liberia’s national security apparatus. They insisted that there is no evidence proving he had prior knowledge that narcotics were being transported.

How Kwabo Became Entangled

Kwabo’s legal troubles emerged from an extensive investigation launched jointly by the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and the Liberia National Police following the discovery of what authorities described as Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking network.

Inspector General of Police Gregory O. W. Coleman disclosed during the investigation that security personnel were allegedly recruited to facilitate the movement of the narcotics from a coastal landing site to a secure holding location.

Investigators concluded that marked Liberia National Police patrol vehicles were allegedly deployed in a two-vehicle escort formation, with one police unit leading and another trailing the convoy transporting the cocaine.

Authorities alleged that Kwabo, then serving as Chief of the Highway Patrol Section, played a central role in coordinating or facilitating that police escort.

The investigation further revealed that the cocaine shipment allegedly entered Liberia through a sophisticated transnational trafficking network involving foreign nationals, including a Serbian national, who investigators say exploited private airstrips and coastal landing points before moving the drugs inland with assistance from local collaborators.

Based on the findings of the Joint National Security Investigative Task Force, Kwabo was arrested, formally charged, and forwarded to court together with Anthony T. Blaye, then Chief of the LNP Financial Crime Division.

Investigators alleged that both officers abused their official positions to protect one of the largest illicit drug shipments ever intercepted in Liberia.

Historic Drug Bust

The investigation represents an unprecedented chapter in Liberia’s anti-drug campaign.

Unlike previous narcotics cases in which public officials were accused of negligence or failure to act, investigators alleged that serving senior police commanders physically participated in transporting cartel drugs using official government vehicles.

Investigators described the operation as highly organized, involving international traffickers, local collaborators, airport-linked operatives, and security personnel.

On July 30, Liberian authorities publicly destroyed approximately 4.2 metric tons of seized cocaine, valued at nearly US$317 million, during what officials described as the country’s largest drug destruction exercise.

The public incineration was intended to demonstrate Liberia’s renewed commitment to dismantling international narcotics networks and to signal that the country would no longer serve as a safe transit point for organized drug trafficking.

Presidential Action

Following the submission of the Joint National Security Investigative Task Force report, President Joseph Nyuma Boakai ordered sweeping disciplinary measures against officials implicated in the investigation.

Among those dismissed were Former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell W. Kwabo, Former Financial Crime Division Chief Anthony T. Blay, and

Several other security and airport officials identified by investigators as having allegedly played various roles in facilitating or failing to prevent the movement of the narcotics.

The President also directed that all individuals identified by investigators be turned over to the appropriate prosecutorial authorities for criminal proceedings. At the same time, additional investigations continued into possible wider networks operating within Liberia’s security institutions and airport system.

The dismissals marked one of the largest disciplinary actions ever taken against serving security personnel over alleged drug trafficking.

Investigation Widens

The investigation has continued to expand beyond the initial arrests.

In recent developments, investigators arrested Moses Jallah, an officer of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency, who is now under investigation for his alleged connection to aspects of the wider narcotics network.

Security has also arrested a prominent private bar owner, George Leroy Henries, who investigators believe may possess information relevant to the movement of suspects and the broader trafficking enterprise.

Both individuals remained under investigation as authorities seek to identify additional local collaborators and determine the full scope of the international criminal network.

Investigators have repeatedly indicated that further arrests remain possible as forensic examinations, financial investigations, telecommunications analyses, and intelligence gathering continue.

Defense Challenges Evidence

However, Kwabo’s lawyers argued that prosecutors have failed to satisfy the constitutional standard required to deny bail.

The motion maintained that no independent evidence connects Kwabo to planning or participating in the alleged conspiracy and argues that the prosecution relies almost exclusively on the statements of an alleged accomplice whose testimony has not been independently corroborated.

The defense further contends that Liberian law requires more than suspicion or association before an accused person may be denied liberty pending trial.

Counsel insists that the prosecution has failed to establish reasonable grounds demonstrating that Kwabo knowingly participated in the trafficking operation or intentionally assisted the principal defendants.

The motion, therefore, requests the court to admit him to bail while awaiting trial.

Case Still Unfolding

Criminal Court “C” has yet to rule on the bail application.

Meanwhile, prosecutors continue building what has become one of the largest organized crime prosecutions in Liberia’s recent history.

With multiple defendants already before the court, additional suspects under active investigation, and security agencies pledging to dismantle every level of the alleged trafficking network, the case continues to expose what investigators believe was a deeply coordinated operation involving international drug traffickers and local collaborators embedded within key state institutions.

The outcome of the prosecution is expected to test the country’s criminal justice system and its resolve to combat transnational organized crime while determining whether senior public officials entrusted with enforcing the law instead became facilitators of one of the country’s largest cocaine trafficking operations.

World.title: Liberia: LDEA OIC Denies Receiving Toyota Pickup From Man Charged in $317M Cocaine Case, Welcomes Independent Probe
World.content:
Monrovia – The Officer-in-Charge of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA), Deputy Commissioner of Police Fitzgerald T. M. Biago, has strongly rejected allegations linking him to individuals accused in Liberia’s multimillion-dollar cocaine trafficking investigation, insisting that he has never accepted gifts, favors or benefits in exchange for compromising his official duties.

By Edwin G. Genoway Jr.

Biago’s denial follows allegations by political activist Martin K. N. Kollie, who claimed in a lengthy social media post that the LDEA chief received a Toyota Hilux pickup truck from George Harris, also known as Leroy Harris, a man reportedly charged by Liberian authorities in connection with the country’s US$317 million cocaine seizure.

Biago dismissed the allegations as false and misleading, saying they are not supported by credible evidence.

“I categorically reject these allegations as false, misleading, and without credible evidence,” Biago stated in a Facebook post.

The LDEA chief said his career has been dedicated to serving Liberia, upholding the law and carrying out his responsibilities with professionalism and integrity.

“I have never accepted any gift, favor, or benefit from any individual or criminal organization in exchange for compromising my duties,” he asserted.

Kollie Questions Toyota Hilux

At the center of Kollie’s allegations is a grey Toyota Hilux pickup truck that he claims is being used by Biago.

Kollie alleged that vehicle registration information he obtained lists George Wha Harris as the registered owner of the pickup, bearing license plate A532084.

According to Kollie, the vehicle was entered into the registration system in November 2024 and registered under Harris’ name. He used the alleged registration information to question how the vehicle came into Biago’s possession and whether it was provided to the LDEA chief by Harris.

However, registration of a vehicle in an individual’s name does not, by itself, establish that the vehicle was subsequently given to another person as a gift or benefit. That claim would require independent verification.

Kollie also alleged that another vehicle was purchased for Biago’s wife by individuals linked to the alleged narcotics network, but the claim was not independently substantiated in the material he published.

Claims of Security Links

Beyond the vehicle allegation, Kollie claimed that Harris maintained relationships with senior security officials, including Biago.

He further alleged that individuals involved in narcotics trafficking had developed relationships within Liberia’s security institutions, particularly the LDEA and the Liberia National Police.

Kollie called for Biago’s resignation or dismissal and urged that the allegations be subjected to a formal investigation.

He also indicated that he intends to release additional information concerning what he described as an alleged drug trafficking network and its suspected collaborators.

Biago Welcomes Investigation

Despite rejecting the allegations, Biago said he is prepared to cooperate with any legitimate investigation by the appropriate authorities.

He stressed, however, that any investigation must be independent, impartial and grounded in evidence rather than social media claims and speculation.

“I remain fully prepared to cooperate with any lawful, independent, and impartial investigation, as I am confident that the truth will prevail through due process rather than speculation or misinformation,” Biago wrote.

His response comes amid heightened public scrutiny of Liberia’s national drug enforcement efforts following major cocaine seizures and ongoing investigations into alleged narcotics trafficking networks.

‘My Focus Remains on the Drug Fight’

Biago said the allegations would not distract him from his responsibilities as head of the LDEA.

He reaffirmed his commitment to combating illicit drug trafficking, dismantling criminal networks and apprehending individuals involved in narcotics-related activities.

“My focus remains steadfast on leading the fight against illicit drugs and dismantling these networks,” he said.

The LDEA has similarly rejected claims that Biago received a vehicle from an alleged drug trafficker, describing the allegation as unsupported by any credible record, documentation or verifiable evidence.

The Agency has encouraged anyone with credible evidence of misconduct to submit it to the appropriate investigative authorities for independent and lawful review.

Allegations Require Verification

The allegations against Biago remain unproven and should not be treated as established facts unless substantiated through an official investigation or judicial proceedings.

The claims presented by Kollie, including the alleged vehicle transfer, do not by themselves establish that Biago participated in drug trafficking, accepted a bribe or committed any criminal offense.

Biago has denied the allegations and has expressly indicated his willingness to face a lawful and independent investigation.

The broader narcotics investigation also remains subject to due process, with individuals accused or charged in connection with the cocaine case entitled to the presumption of innocence unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

For Biago, however, the message is clear: he says the allegations will not deter him from leading Liberia’s fight against illicit drugs.

“My focus remains steadfast on leading the fight against illicit drugs and dismantling these networks,” he said.

World.title: Liberia: LDEA Dismisses Claims OIC Biago Received Pickup From Alleged Drug Trafficker
World.content:
Monrovia – The Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) has rejected allegations that its Officer-in-Charge, Deputy Commissioner of Police Fitzgerald T. M. Biago received a Toyota pickup truck from an individual allegedly linked to drug trafficking.

The allegations were made by political activist Martin K. N. Kollie, who claimed that the LDEA chief received benefits from individuals connected to an alleged cocaine trafficking network.

In a lengthy social media post, Kollie further alleged that George Wha Harris, also known as Leroy Harris, who has been charged in connection with an ongoing narcotics investigation, maintained relationships with senior security officials, including Biago.

The allegations have since circulated widely on social media and other platforms.

However, in a press release issued Friday, August 7, the LDEA described the claim as false, maintaining that it has not been supported by any verifiable evidence.

The Agency said Biago, who serves as a Deputy Commissioner of Police, categorically denies receiving or accepting the vehicle described in the allegation. According to the LDEA, he also did not authorize anyone to receive the vehicle on his behalf.

“The LDEA is not aware of any credible record, documentation, or evidence substantiating the claim,” the Agency said.

The drug enforcement agency acknowledged that public officials must remain subject to legitimate scrutiny, while urging anyone with credible evidence of misconduct to submit it to the appropriate investigative authorities for independent investigation.

“The LDEA recognizes that public officials must remain open to legitimate scrutiny. For that reason, any person possessing credible evidence of misconduct is encouraged to submit it to the appropriate investigative authority for an independent and lawful review,” the statement said.

The Agency emphasized that serious allegations should be tested against evidence and due process rather than repeated as established facts without verification.

The LDEA also reaffirmed its “zero tolerance” policy toward corruption, misconduct and collusion with criminal networks, stressing that the standard applies to every officer regardless of rank.

“These standards apply to every officer, regardless of rank, and any substantiated violation will be addressed in accordance with law and established disciplinary procedures,” the Agency said.

The LDEA further appealed to the public and media to verify allegations before publishing or sharing them, particularly when unsubstantiated claims could prejudice ongoing investigations, damage reputations or undermine public confidence in national security institutions.

The Agency clarified that its call for verification is not intended to restrict lawful criticism or responsible journalism, but rather to reinforce what it described as the shared responsibility to distinguish allegations from established facts.

As Liberia intensifies its efforts to combat drug trafficking, the LDEA urged members of the public to continue reporting suspicious activities through its hotlines: 0777-133-333 / 0888-133-333.

World.title: How a Paynesville Nightspot Became Ground Zero in Liberia’s Cocaine Case
World.content:
Monrovia – The operation that shut down Private Bar on Wednesday looked, from the outside, like a raid built to send a message. Heavily armed security officers blocked access to the premises as investigators moved through the property, and journalists who arrived at the scene were kept at a distance on the instructions of a senior female LDEA officer overseeing the operation.
